title.zh: 卷三十一 列傳第二十一 張裕
title.raw: 卷三十一 列傳第二十一 張裕 Volume 31 Biographies 21: Zhang Yu

sentences.zh: 茂度仕為宋武帝太尉主簿、揚州中從事，累遷別駕。

translations.literal: Maodu served as Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant under Emperor Wu of Song and as Middle Attendant of Yang Province, rising through the ranks to become Vice Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Maodu served on Liu Yu’s staff as chief clerk to the grand commandant and as middle attendant of Yang Province, eventually rising to vice governor.

sentences.zh: 武帝西伐劉毅，北伐關洛，皆居守留任州事。

translations.literal: When the Emperor marched west against Liu Yi and north against Guan and Luo, Maodu remained behind to hold the province and manage its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Liu Yu’s campaigns west against Liu Yi and north toward Guan and Luo, Maodu stayed behind to govern Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 出為都督、廣州刺史、平越中郎將，綏靜百越，嶺外安之。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Area Commander, Governor of Guang Province, and General of the Center Who Pacifies the Yue; he soothed the hundred Yue peoples and brought peace beyond the Ling range.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as area commander, governor of Guang Province, and general who pacified the Yue, he quieted the southern tribes and secured the lands beyond the Ling Mountains.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年，為侍中、都督、益州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia, he became Attendant-in-Ordinary, Area Commander, and Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 1 he was made attendant-in-ordinary, area commander, and governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 帝討荊州刺史謝晦，詔益州遣軍襲江陵。

translations.literal: When the Emperor attacked Jing Province Governor Xie Hui, he ordered Yi Province to send troops in a raid on Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved against Xie Hui, governor of Jing Province, he ordered troops from Yi Province to strike at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 晦平，西軍始至白帝。

translations.literal: After Hui was suppressed, the western army only then reached Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was already defeated before the western army even reached Baidi.

sentences.zh: 茂度與晦素善，議者疑其出軍遲留。

translations.literal: Maodu had long been on good terms with Hui, and critics suspected him of delaying his march.
translations.idiomatic: Because Maodu and Hui had been close, some accused him of deliberately slow marching.

sentences.zh: 弟邵時為湘州刺史，起兵應大駕。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shao was then Governor of Xiang Province and raised troops in response to the imperial campaign.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shao, then governor of Xiang Province, mobilized in support of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上以邵誠節，故不加罪。

translations.literal: Because the Emperor regarded Shao’s loyalty as sincere, he imposed no punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared Maodu punishment, crediting Shao’s loyal response.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常，以腳疾出為義興太守。

translations.literal: Maodu rose to Minister of Ceremonies, then because of a foot ailment was sent out as Governor of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to minister of ceremonies, he later left office for a foot ailment and became governor of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 上從容謂曰：「勿以西蜀介懷。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to him at ease, “Do not let western Shu weigh on your mind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reassured him: “Do not brood over what happened in western Shu.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣不遭陛下之明，墓木拱矣。」

translations.literal: ” He replied, “Had I not met Your Majesty’s clear judgment, the trees over my grave would already be tall.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Maodu answered, “Without Your Majesty’s fairness, I would already be dead and buried.”

sentences.zh: 後為都官尚書，以疾就拜光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: Later he became Director of the Ministry of Justice; because of illness he accepted appointment as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple sash.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as director of the ministry of justice, then accepted the post of grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple sash while ill.

sentences.zh: 茂度內足於財，自絕人事，經始本縣之華山為居止。

translations.literal: Maodu was inwardly content with his wealth, withdrew from worldly affairs, and began building a residence on Mount Hua in his home county.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy enough for his needs, he withdrew from public life and built a home on Mount Hua in his native county.

sentences.zh: 優遊野澤，如此者七年。

translations.literal: He wandered freely in marshes and wilds in this way for seven years.
translations.idiomatic: For seven years he lived at ease among marshes and open country.

sentences.zh: 十八年，除會稽太守。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was made governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 素有吏能，職事甚理。

translations.literal: He had long possessed administrative talent, and his official duties were very well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Already known for administrative skill, he governed with notable efficiency.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，諡曰恭子。

translations.literal: He died in office; his posthumous title was Gongzi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously titled Gongzi.

sentences.zh: 子 演

translations.literal: Son: Yan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yan

sentences.zh: 子演，位太子中舍人。

translations.literal: Yan held the post of Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan rose to attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 演四弟鏡、永、辯、岱俱知名，時謂之「張氏五龍」。

translations.literal: Yan’s four younger brothers Jing, Yong, Bian, and Dai were all well known; people of the time called them “the Five Dragons of the Zhang clan.”
translations.idiomatic: Yan’s four younger brothers—Jing, Yong, Bian, and Dai—were all celebrated; contemporaries called them the Five Dragons of the Zhang clan.

sentences.zh: 子 鏡

translations.literal: Son: Jing
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jing

sentences.zh: 鏡少與光祿大夫顏延之鄰居，顏談義飲酒，喧呼不絕，而鏡靜默無言聲。

translations.literal: In youth Jing lived next to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Yan Yanzhi; Yan would discuss doctrine and drink wine with unceasing clamor, while Jing remained silent and made no sound.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Jing lived beside Yan Yanzhi, who held forth on doctrine over wine with endless noise while Jing sat in wordless silence.

sentences.zh: 後鏡與客談，延之從籬邊聞之，取胡床坐聽，辭義清玄。

translations.literal: Later, when Jing was conversing with a guest, Yanzhi heard him from beyond the hedge, took a folding stool, and sat listening; Jing’s words and meaning were clear and subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Once, hearing Jing talk with a guest from the other side of the hedge, Yanzhi brought a folding stool to listen and found his discourse lucid and refined.

sentences.zh: 延之心服，謂客曰：「彼有人焉。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was convinced at heart and said to the guest, “There is a man in him.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed, Yanzhi told the guest, “This man has real substance.

sentences.zh: 」由是不復酣叫。

translations.literal: ” From then on he no longer shouted drunkenly.
translations.idiomatic: ” After that he never again roared in drunken debate.

sentences.zh: 仕至新安太守。

translations.literal: In office he rose to Governor of Xin’an.
translations.idiomatic: In service he became governor of Xin’an.

sentences.zh: 演、鏡兄弟中名最高，餘並不及。

translations.literal: Among Yan and Jing’s brothers their fame stood highest; the rest did not match them.
translations.idiomatic: Of the brothers, Yan and Jing enjoyed the greatest renown.

sentences.zh: 初，裕曾祖澄當葬父，郭璞為占墓地，曰：「葬某處，年過百歲，位至三司，而子孫不蕃。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yu’s great-grandfather Cheng was about to bury his father, Guo Pu cast the grave site and said, “If buried at a certain place, one will live past a hundred years and reach the rank of the Three Excellencies, but descendants will not flourish.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu’s great-grandfather Cheng prepared to bury his father, Guo Pu divined the site and said, “One spot promises a life beyond a hundred years and rank among the Three Excellencies, but few descendants.

sentences.zh: 某處年幾減半，位裁卿校，而累世貴顯。

translations.literal: At another place the years are nearly halved and the rank only reaches commandery and garrison commander, yet generation after generation will be noble and prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Another spot cuts the lifespan nearly in half and caps rank at commandery or garrison commander, yet the line will flourish for generations.

sentences.zh: 」澄乃葬其劣處。

translations.literal: ” Cheng then buried him at the lesser site.
translations.idiomatic: ” Cheng chose the lesser site.

sentences.zh: 位光祿，年六十四而亡，其子孫遂昌云。

translations.literal: He reached the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, died at sixty-four, and his descendants thereafter prospered.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand master of splendid happiness, died at sixty-four, and his line thereafter flourished.

sentences.zh: 子 永

translations.literal: Son: Yong
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yong

sentences.zh: 永字景雲，初為郡主簿，累遷尚書中兵郎。

translations.literal: Yong, styled Jingyun, first served as chief clerk of a commandery and rose through the ranks to Lang of Central Troops in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, styled Jingyun, began as a commandery chief clerk and rose to lang of central troops in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 先是尚書中條制繁雜，元嘉十八年，欲加修撰，徙永為刪定郎，掌其任。

translations.literal: Previously the regulations of the Ministry were numerous and complex; in the eighteenth year of Yuanjia the court wished to revise them, and Yong was transferred to the post of Editing and Fixing Lang to take charge of the task.
translations.idiomatic: Because ministry regulations had grown tangled, in Yuanjia 18 the court set out to revise them and put Yong in charge as editing-and-fixing lang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，除建康令，所居皆有稱績。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Magistrate of Jiankang; in every post he held he won praise for his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he became magistrate of Jiankang and earned a reputation in every office he held.

sentences.zh: 又除廣陵王誕北中郎錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was also appointed Recording Secretary under Prince of Guangling Dan’s Northern Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as recording secretary on Prince of Guangling Dan’s northern staff.

sentences.zh: 永涉獵書史，能為文章，善隸書，騎射雜藝，觸類兼善。

translations.literal: Yong ranged widely through books and histories, could compose literary works, was skilled at clerical script, and excelled at riding, archery, and assorted arts—whatever he touched he mastered.
translations.idiomatic: Yong read widely in history, wrote well, mastered clerical script, and was adept at riding, archery, and every art he attempted.

sentences.zh: 又有巧思，益為文帝所知。

translations.literal: He also had ingenious ideas and came increasingly to be known by Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His ingenuity brought him increasingly to Emperor Wen’s attention.

sentences.zh: 紙墨皆自營造，上每得永表啟，輒執玩咨嗟，自歎供禦者了不及也。

translations.literal: He made his own paper and ink; whenever the Emperor received Yong’s memorials he would take them in hand, admire them, and sigh that even the imperial supply office fell far short.
translations.idiomatic: He even made his own paper and ink; the emperor would linger over Yong’s memorials and marvel that the imperial workshops could not match them.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，造華林園、玄武湖，並使永監統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the construction of Hualin Garden and Xuanwu Lake was entrusted to Yong’s overall supervision.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he oversaw construction of Hualin Garden and Xuanwu Lake.

sentences.zh: 凡所制置，皆受則於永。

translations.literal: In every arrangement made, the court took Yong’s plans as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Every design followed Yong’s specifications.

sentences.zh: 永既有才能，每盡心力，文帝謂堪為將。

translations.literal: Since Yong had both talent and ability and always gave his full effort, Emperor Wen said he was fit to be a general.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, impressed by Yong’s talent and tireless effort, judged him capable of military command.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以永為揚威將軍、冀州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Yong was made General Who Displays Might and Governor of Ji Province, with the added title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was made general who displays might and governor of Ji Province, with area command.

sentences.zh: 督王玄謨、申坦等諸將經略河南，進攻碻磝，累旬不拔，為魏軍所殺甚眾。

translations.literal: He directed Wang Xuanmo, Shen Tan, and other generals in operations on the south bank of the Yellow River, advancing to attack Quebo; for many ten-day periods they could not take it, and Wei troops killed very many of their men.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding Wang Xuanmo, Shen Tan, and others on the south bank of the Yellow River, he besieged Quebo for weeks without success while Wei forces slaughtered his troops in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 永即夜撤圍退軍，不報告諸將，眾軍驚擾，為魏所乘，死敗塗地。

translations.literal: Yong that night withdrew the siege and retreated without informing the other generals; the armies were thrown into alarm and disorder and were overrun by Wei—dead and defeated men covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yong pulled back by night without warning the other commanders; panic spread, Wei forces fell upon them, and the field was heaped with dead.

sentences.zh: 永及申坦並為統府撫軍將軍蕭思話所收，系於曆城獄。

translations.literal: Yong and Shen Tan were both taken into custody by Pacifying Army General Xiao Sihua of the supreme command and imprisoned in Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua, pacifying army general of the supreme command, seized Yong and Shen Tan and jailed them at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 文帝以屢征無功，諸將不可任，詔責永等與思話。

translations.literal: Because repeated campaigns had achieved nothing and the generals could not be entrusted with command, Emperor Wen issued an edict rebuking Yong and the others along with Sihua.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated by repeated failure, Emperor Wen rebuked Yong, Shen Tan, and Sihua by edict.

sentences.zh: 又與江夏王義恭書曰：「早知諸將輩如此，恨不以白刃驅之，今者悔何所及。」

translations.literal: He also wrote to Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, saying, “Had I known earlier that this generation of generals would be like this, I would regret not driving them on with naked blades—what regret can there be now?”
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Prince of Jiangxia Yigong: “Had I known these generals would fail so miserably, I would have driven them with the sword itself—too late for regret now.”

sentences.zh: 三十年，元凶弑立，起永為青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, after the crown prince’s regicide and usurpation, Yong was summoned to be Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince’s regicide in the thirtieth year, Yong was recalled to govern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 及司空南譙王義宣起義，又改永為冀州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When Minister of Works Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan raised the righteous banner, Yong was again changed to Governor of Ji Province with the added title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan rose in revolt, Yong was reassigned as governor of Ji Province with area command.

sentences.zh: 永遣司馬崔勳之、中兵參軍劉宣則二軍馳赴國難。

translations.literal: Yong sent two armies under Marshal Cui Xunzhi and Central Troops Aide Liu Xuanze to hurry to the capital’s defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yong dispatched two forces under Cui Xunzhi and Liu Xuanze to rush to the capital’s aid.

sentences.zh: 時蕭思話在彭城，義宣慮二人不相諧緝，與思話書，勸與永坦懷。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Sihua was at Pengcheng; Yixuan feared the two men would not work in harmony and wrote Sihua urging open-hearted cooperation with Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua was then at Pengcheng; fearing discord, Yixuan wrote urging him to reconcile with Yong.

sentences.zh: 又使永從兄長史張暢與永書勖之，使遠慕廉、藺在公之德，近效平、勃亡私之美。

translations.literal: He also had Yong’s elder cousin Chief Clerk Zhang Chang write to Yong encouraging him to look far to the public virtue of Lian and Lin and near to the selfless excellence of Ping and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Yong’s cousin Zhang Chang write urging him to emulate the public loyalty of Lian Po and Lin Xiangru and the selfless service of Chen Ping and Zhou Bo.

sentences.zh: 事平，召為江夏王義恭大司馬從事中郎，領中兵。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Yong was summoned as Senior Aide on the Grand Marshal’s staff of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, with concurrent command of central troops.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion ended, Yong joined Prince of Jiangxia Yigong’s grand marshal staff as senior aide and commanded central troops.

sentences.zh: 孝武孝建元年，臧質反，遣永輔武昌王渾鎮京口。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, when Zang Zhi rebelled, Yong was sent to assist Prince of Wuchang Hun in guarding Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 1, when Zang Zhi rebelled, Yong helped Prince of Wuchang Hun hold Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，累遷廷尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming he rose through the ranks to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 3 he became minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 上謂曰：「卿既與釋之同姓，欲使天下復無冤人。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to him, “You share a surname with [Zhang] Shizhi; I wish to make the realm again free of the wrongfully condemned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, “You bear the same surname as Zhang Shizhi; I want the empire again to know no innocent condemned.

sentences.zh: 」永曉音律，太極殿前鐘聲嘶，孝武嘗以問永。

translations.literal: ” Yong understood musical pitch; when the bell before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate gave a hoarse tone, Emperor Xiaowu once questioned Yong about it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong knew music; when the bell before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate sounded hoarse, Emperor Xiaowu asked his opinion.

sentences.zh: 永答鍾有銅滓，乃扣鍾求其處，鑿而去之，聲遂清越。

translations.literal: Yong answered that the bell had copper slag; he struck the bell to find the spot, chiseled it away, and the tone became clear and resonant.
translations.idiomatic: Yong said copper dross was the cause, found the flaw by tapping the bell, scraped it out, and restored a clear tone.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，為青冀二州刺史，監四州諸軍事，統諸將討徐州刺史薛安都，累戰克捷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, Yong became Governor of Qing and Ji Provinces, overseeing military affairs in four provinces and commanding the generals against Xu Province Governor Xue Andu; in repeated battles he won victories.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he governed Qing and Ji, commanded four provinces, and led repeated victories against Xue Andu of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 破薛索兒。

translations.literal: He defeated Xue Suo’er.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Xue Suo’er.

sentences.zh: 又遷鎮軍將軍，尋為南兗州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Stabilizes the Army, then became Governor of Southern Yan Province with the added title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to general who stabilizes the army, he then governed Southern Yan with area command.

sentences.zh: 時薛安都據彭城請降，而誠心不款。

translations.literal: At that time Xue Andu held Pengcheng and offered surrender, but his sincerity was not whole-hearted.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu then held Pengcheng and offered surrender, but his loyalty was doubtful.

sentences.zh: 明帝遣永與沈攸之重兵迎之，加都督前鋒諸軍事，進軍彭城。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Yong and Shen Youzhi with a heavy force to welcome him, adding to Yong command over the vanguard armies; they advanced on Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Yong and Shen Youzhi with a large force to receive him, putting Yong in command of the vanguard as they marched on Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 安都招引魏兵既至，永狼狽引軍還，為魏軍追大敗，復遇寒雪，士卒離散。

translations.literal: Andu had already summoned Wei troops; Yong withdrew his army in disarray, was heavily defeated in pursuit by Wei troops, and then met with cold snow—soldiers scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Andu had already called in Wei troops; Yong fled in disorder, was routed in pursuit, and a bitter snowstorm scattered what remained of his army.

sentences.zh: 永腳指斷落，僅以身免，失其第四子。

translations.literal: Yong’s toes were severed; he barely escaped with his life and lost his fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Toes torn off, he barely escaped alive and lost his fourth son.

sentences.zh: 三年，徙會稽太守，加都督，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Governor of Kuaiji with the added title of Area Commander; his general’s rank remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was moved to Kuaiji as governor with area command, retaining his general’s rank.

sentences.zh: 以北行失律，固求自貶，降號左將軍。

translations.literal: Because of his failure on the northern campaign he firmly sought self-demotion and was reduced to the rank of Left General.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of the northern debacle, he insisted on demotion and was reduced to left general.

sentences.zh: 永痛悼所失之子，有兼常哀，服制雖除，猶立靈座，飲食衣服，待之如生。

translations.literal: Yong grieved deeply for the son he had lost; his mourning exceeded the ordinary. Though the mourning period had ended, he still kept a spirit seat, and in food and clothing treated him as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his lost son with extraordinary grief; even after mourning ended he kept a spirit seat and served food and clothing as though the boy still lived.

sentences.zh: 每出行，常別具名車好馬，號曰侍從。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out, he would separately prepare a fine carriage and good horses, calling them his attendant retinue.
translations.idiomatic: On outings he always set out a fine carriage and horses for the dead boy, calling them his son’s escort.

sentences.zh: 有軍事，輒語左右報郎君知也。

translations.literal: When there was military business he would tell his attendants to inform “the young master.”
translations.idiomatic: When military matters arose he would tell attendants, “Let the young master know.”

sentences.zh: 以破薛索兒功，封孝昌縣侯。

translations.literal: For his merit in defeating Xue Suo’er he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaochang.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Xue Suo’er he was enfeoffed as marquis of Xiaochang.

sentences.zh: 在會稽，賓客有謝方童、阮須、何達之等竊其權，贓貨盈積。

translations.literal: While in Kuaiji, guests Xie Fangtong, Ruan Xu, and He Dazhi usurped his authority, and bribes piled up.
translations.idiomatic: At Kuaiji his clients Xie Fangtong, Ruan Xu, and He Dazhi seized power for themselves and amassed illicit wealth.

sentences.zh: 方童等坐贓下獄死，永又降號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Fangtong and the others were convicted of bribery, imprisoned, and executed; Yong was again reduced to the rank of General Who Triumphs.
translations.idiomatic: Fangtong and the others were executed for corruption; Yong was demoted again to general who triumphs.

sentences.zh: 子 岱

translations.literal: Son: Dai
translations.idiomatic: Son: Dai

sentences.zh: 岱字景山，州辟從事，累遷東遷令。

translations.literal: Dai, styled Jingshan, was recruited as a staff aide of the province and rose through the ranks to Magistrate of Dongqian.
translations.idiomatic: Dai, styled Jingshan, entered service as a provincial aide and became magistrate of Dongqian.

sentences.zh: 時殷沖為吳興太守，謂人曰：「張東遷親貧須養，所以棲遲下邑。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Chong was Governor of Wuxing and said to others, “Magistrate Zhang of Dongqian is close to poverty and must support his family, and so he lingers in a small county.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chong, governor of Wuxing, remarked, “Magistrate Zhang of Dongqian is poor and must support kin—that is why he stays in a small county.

sentences.zh: 然名器方顯，終當大至。」

translations.literal: Yet his reputation and office are just emerging; in the end he will rise very high.”
translations.idiomatic: But his name is rising; he will go far.”

sentences.zh: 後為司徒左西曹掾。

translations.literal: Later he became Senior Aide of the Left in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as senior aide of the left in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 母年八十，籍注未滿，岱便去官，從實還養。

translations.literal: His mother was eighty, and though his registered mourning term was not complete, Dai at once left office and returned home in truth to support her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was eighty; though his mourning term on the register was incomplete, he resigned at once to care for her.

sentences.zh: 有司以岱違制，將欲糾舉。

translations.literal: The relevant office, because Dai had violated regulations, was about to investigate and report him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials prepared to charge him for breaking mourning regulations.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武曰：「觀過可以知仁，不須案也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song said, “From a fault one can know a man’s humanity; there is no need for an inquiry.”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu said, “His breach shows his filial heart; let the matter drop.”

sentences.zh: 累遷山陰令，職事閑理。

translations.literal: He rose through the ranks to Magistrate of Shanyin; his official duties were calmly well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to magistrate of Shanyin, he governed with quiet competence.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王休若為北徐州，未親政事，以岱為冠軍諮議參軍，領彭城太守，行府、州、國事。

translations.literal: When Prince of Baling Xiuru became Northern Governor of Xu Province and had not yet taken charge of government affairs himself, Dai was made Senior Adviser of the Champion and concurrent Governor of Pengcheng, handling the princely residence, provincial, and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Baling Xiuru governed northern Xu but did not yet handle affairs himself, Dai served as his senior adviser and acting governor of Pengcheng, running princely, provincial, and state business.

sentences.zh: 後臨海王為征虜將軍廣州，豫章王為車騎揚州，晉安王為征虜南兗州，岱曆為三府諮議三王行事，與典簽主帥共事，事舉而情得。

translations.literal: Later when Prince of Linhai served as General Who Conquers the Barbarians at Guangzhou, Prince of Yuzhang as Chariots and Cavalry at Yangzhou, and Prince of Jin’an as General Who Conquers the Barbarians at Southern Yan, Dai successively served as senior adviser to all three princes and handled their affairs together with the registry clerks and commanders—when business was done, feeling was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He later acted for three successive princes—Linhai at Guangzhou, Yuzhang at Yangzhou, Jin’an at Southern Yan—working with registry staff and commanders so that affairs were settled without rancor.

sentences.zh: 或謂岱曰：「主王既幼，執事多門，而每能緝和公私，云何致此？

translations.literal: Some said to Dai, “The princes are still young and many hands hold power; yet you always harmonize public and private affairs—how do you achieve this?
translations.idiomatic: People asked Dai, “These princes are young and many factions compete for power—how do you always reconcile public duty and private feeling?

sentences.zh: 」岱曰：「古人言，一心可以事百君。

translations.literal: ” Dai said, “The ancients said that with one heart one may serve a hundred lords.
translations.idiomatic: ” He answered, “The ancients said one loyal heart can serve a hundred masters.

sentences.zh: 我為政端平，待物以禮，悔吝之事，無由而及；

translations.literal: I govern uprightly and treat people with ritual; matters of regret have no way to reach me;
translations.idiomatic: I govern fairly and treat people with courtesy, leaving no cause for regret;

sentences.zh: 明闇短長，更是才用多少耳。」

translations.literal: whether a lord is bright or dark, short or long in talent, is simply a matter of how much ability he has.”
translations.idiomatic: whether a prince succeeds or fails is only a question of his own capacity.”

sentences.zh: 入為黃門郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 新安王子鸞以盛寵為南徐州，割吳郡屬焉。

translations.literal: Prince of Xin’an Ziluan, because of exceptional favor, was made Southern Governor of Xu; Wu Commandery was carved out and placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xin’an Ziluan, greatly favored, became southern governor of Xu, with Wu Commandery attached to his domain.

sentences.zh: 高選佐史，孝武召岱謂曰：「卿美效夙著，兼資宦已多，今欲用卿為子鸞別駕，總刺史之任，無謂小屈，終當大申也。

translations.literal: Senior aides were chosen with great care; Emperor Xiaowu summoned Dai and said, “Your fine achievements have long been evident and you have already served widely in office; I now wish to appoint you Vice Governor to Ziluan to oversee the governor’s duties—do not think this too small a post; in the end you will be greatly advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Dai and said, “Your record is long and distinguished; I mean to make you Ziluan’s vice governor with full charge of the province—take this not as a slight, for greater honors will follow.

sentences.zh: 」帝崩，累遷吏部郎。

translations.literal: ” After the Emperor died, Dai rose through the ranks to Lang of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: ” After the emperor’s death he rose to lang in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 泰始末，為吳興太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Taishi he became Governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taishi he governed Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，為益州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: During Yuanhui he became Governor of Yi Province with the added title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhui he governed Yi Province with area command.

sentences.zh: 數年，益土安其政。

translations.literal: After several years the people of Yi were settled under his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Yi Province prospered under his rule.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He rose through the ranks to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 王儉為吏部郎，時專斷曹事，岱每相違執。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian was Lang of the Ministry of Personnel he monopolized bureau business; Dai often opposed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian as lang monopolized personnel decisions; Dai frequently blocked him.

sentences.zh: 及儉為宰相，以此頗不相善。

translations.literal: When Jian became chief minister, because of this they were rather ill disposed toward each other.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian became chief minister, their mutual dislike deepened.

sentences.zh: 兄子瑰、弟恕誅吳郡太守劉遐，齊高帝欲以恕為晉陵郡。

translations.literal: His nephew Gui and younger brother Shu killed Wu Commandery Governor Liu Xia; Emperor Gao of Qi wished to appoint Shu as governor of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When his nephew Gui and brother Shu killed Governor Liu Xia of Wu Commandery, Emperor Gao wanted to make Shu governor of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 岱曰：「恕未閑從政，美錦不宜濫裁。

translations.literal: Dai said, “Shu is not yet practiced in governing; fine brocade should not be cut carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Dai objected: “Shu lacks governing experience; fine brocade should not be cut rashly.

sentences.zh: 」高帝曰：「恕為人我所悉，其又與瑰同勳，自應有賞。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “I know Shu’s character well, and since he shares Gui’s merit he should naturally be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor replied, “I know Shu, and he shares Gui’s service—he deserves reward.

sentences.zh: 」岱曰：「若以家貧賜祿，此所不論；

translations.literal: ” Dai said, “If salary is granted because the family is poor, that is not what I discuss;
translations.idiomatic: ” Dai said, “If you mean salary because we are poor, say so;

sentences.zh: 語功推事，臣門之恥。

translations.literal: to speak of merit and push office is a shame to my house.”
translations.idiomatic: but to reward office for this deed shames our clan.”

sentences.zh: 」加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，中詔序朝臣，欲以右僕射擬岱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan an imperial order ranked the court ministers and intended to place Dai as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 1 a court ranking would have placed Dai as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 褚彥回謂得此過優，若別有忠誠，特宜升引者，別是一理。

translations.literal: Chu Yanhui said this was too generous; if there were separate loyalty deserving special promotion, that would be another matter.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui said that was too high unless separate loyalty justified special advancement.

sentences.zh: 」詔更量。

translations.literal: ” The edict was revised.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was revised.

sentences.zh: 出為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高帝知岱歷任清直，至郡未幾，手敕曰：「大郡任重，乃未欲回換，但總戎務殷，宜須望實。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew Dai’s successive posts had been pure and upright; not long after he reached the commandery, he wrote by hand, “A great commandery’s burden is weighty, and I am not yet ready to transfer you, but overall military affairs are pressing and solid reputation is needed.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Dai’s record of integrity, the emperor soon wrote: “Wu is a great commandery and I am not ready to move you, but military affairs demand proven merit.

sentences.zh: 今用卿為護軍。

translations.literal: I now appoint you Defender of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: I appoint you defender of the army.

sentences.zh: 加給事中。

translations.literal: He was additionally given the title Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made attendant.

sentences.zh: 」岱拜竟，詔以家為府。

translations.literal: ” When Dai had completed his audience, an edict made his home his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After his audience, an edict made his residence his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 武

translations.literal: Wu
translations.idiomatic: Wu

sentences.zh: 帝即位，復為吳興太守。

translations.literal: When the Emperor acceded, Dai again became Governor of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu acceded, Dai again governed Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 岱晚節在吳興，更以寬恕著名。

translations.literal: In his later years at Wuxing, Dai became still more famous for leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years at Wuxing he grew famous for clemency.

sentences.zh: 遷南兗州刺史，未拜卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Southern Yan Province but died before accepting the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to southern Yan, he died before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 岱初作遺命，分張家財，封置箱中，家業張減，隨復改易，如此十數年。

translations.literal: Early on Dai made a testament dividing the Zhang family property, sealing it in a chest; as the family estate shrank he repeatedly revised it in this way for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He had long since drawn up a will dividing family property in a sealed chest, revising it again and again over more than a decade as estates changed.

sentences.zh: 諡曰貞子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhenzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Zhenzi.

sentences.zh: 演子 緒

translations.literal: Yan’s son: Xu
translations.idiomatic: Yan’s son: Xu

sentences.zh: 緒字思曼，岱兄子也。

translations.literal: Xu, styled Siman, was Dai’s elder brother’s son.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, styled Siman, was Dai’s nephew.

sentences.zh: 父演，宋太子中舍人。

translations.literal: His father Yan held the post of Attendant of the Heir Apparent in Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan had been attendant of the heir apparent under Song.

sentences.zh: 緒少知名，清簡寡欲，從伯敷及叔父鏡、從叔暢並貴異之。

translations.literal: Xu was known from youth for purity and simplicity and few desires; his uncle Fu and his uncles Jing and Chang all regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Known from youth for purity and restraint, he was prized by his uncle Fu and his uncles Jing and Chang.

sentences.zh: 鏡比之樂廣，敷云：「是我輩人」。

translations.literal: Jing compared him to Yue Guang; Fu said, “He is one of our kind.”
translations.idiomatic: Jing compared him to Yue Guang; Fu said, “He is one of us.”

sentences.zh: 暢言于孝武帝，用為尚書倉部郎。

translations.literal: Chang spoke of him to Emperor Xiaowu, who appointed him Lang of the Granary Section in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Chang recommended him to Emperor Xiaowu, who made him lang of the granary section.

sentences.zh: 都令史諮詳郡縣米事，緒蕭然直視，不以經懷。

translations.literal: When the chief clerks consulted on commandery and county grain matters, Xu sat aloof and looked straight ahead, not taking it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks debated grain accounts, Xu sat detached and unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝每見緒，輒歎其清淡。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Ming of Song saw Xu he would sigh at his pure detachment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sighed each time he saw Xu’s austere bearing.

sentences.zh: 轉太子中庶子、本州大中正，遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Arbiter of his native province, then moved to Senior Aide of the Left in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became senior mentor of the heir apparent and grand arbiter of his province, then senior aide of the left.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書袁粲言於帝曰：「臣觀張緒有正始遺風，宜為宮職。

translations.literal: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Yuan Can said to the Emperor, “I observe that Zhang Xu carries the surviving style of the Zhengshi era and should hold palace office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can told the emperor, “Zhang Xu has the detached spirit of the Zhengshi age and belongs in palace office.

sentences.zh: 」復轉中庶子。

translations.literal: ” He was again transferred to Senior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: ” He returned to senior mentor.

sentences.zh: 後為侍中，遷吏部郎，參掌大選。

translations.literal: Later he became Attendant-in-Ordinary, then Lang of the Ministry of Personnel, sharing charge of major appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He later became attendant-in-ordinary, then lang of personnel, sharing major appointments.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，東宮官罷，選曹擬舍人王儉為格外記室。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui, when eastern palace offices were abolished, the Selection Bureau proposed Attendant Wang Jian as extraordinary recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanhui’s start, with eastern palace posts abolished, personnel proposed Wang Jian as extraordinary recorder.

sentences.zh: 緒以儉人地兼美，宜轉秘書丞。

translations.literal: Xu, because Jian’s person and background were both excellent, said he should be transferred to secretary director.
translations.idiomatic: Xu argued that Jian’s talent and pedigree suited the secretary directorship instead.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 緒又遷侍中，嘗私謂客曰：「一生不解作諾。

translations.literal: Xu was again transferred to Attendant and once privately said to a guest, “In all my life I have not understood how to say yes.
translations.idiomatic: Again made attendant, he once told a guest, “I have never learned to say yes.

sentences.zh: 」有以告袁粲、褚彥回者，由是出為吳郡太守，緒初不知也。

translations.literal: ” When this was reported to Yuan Can and Chu Yanhui, he was sent out as Governor of Wu Commandery without Xu’s knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: ” When Yuan Can and Chu Yanhui heard, he was exiled to Wu Commandery without being told.

sentences.zh: 駕幸莊嚴寺聽僧達道人講維摩，坐遠不聞緒言，上難移緒，乃遷僧達以近之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Zhuangyan Temple to hear the monk Dadao expound the Vimalakirti Sutra, Xu sat too far away to hear; the Emperor, unwilling to move Xu, transferred Dadao closer.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuangyan Temple the emperor heard Dadao preach the Vimalakirti Sutra; rather than move Xu farther back, he moved the monk closer.

sentences.zh: 時帝欲用緒為右僕射，以問王儉。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor wished to appoint Xu Right Vice Director and questioned Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then considered Xu for right vice director and asked Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「緒少有清望，誠美選也。

translations.literal: Jian said, “Xu from youth has enjoyed pure repute; he is truly a fine choice.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, “Xu’s pure reputation makes him an excellent choice.

sentences.zh: 南士由來少居此職。

translations.literal: Southern men have seldom held this office.
translations.idiomatic: Southerners rarely hold that post.

sentences.zh: 」褚彥回曰：「儉少年或未憶耳，江左用陸玩、顧和，皆南人也。

translations.literal: ” Chu Yanhui said, “Jian is young and perhaps does not remember: in the Jiangzuo era Lu Wan and Gu He were appointed, and both were southern men.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chu Yanhui replied, “Jian may be too young to recall Lu Wan and Gu He under the eastern Jin.

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「晉氏衰政，不可為則。

translations.literal: ” Jian said, “The Jin court’s decadent governance cannot serve as a model.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jian answered, “Decadent Jin is no model.

sentences.zh: 」先是緒諸子皆輕俠，中子充少時又不護細行，儉又以為言，乃止。

translations.literal: ” Earlier Xu’s sons had all been frivolous; his middle son Chong in youth also did not guard small conduct, and Jian spoke of this too, so the appointment stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jian also cited Xu’s unruly sons, especially Chong, and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 及立國學，以緒為太常卿，領國子祭酒，以王延之代緒為中書令。

translations.literal: When the National University was established, Xu was made Minister of Ceremonies and concurrently Director of the National University; Wang Yanzhi replaced Xu as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the National University was founded, Xu became minister of ceremonies and director of the university; Wang Yanzhi replaced him in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 何點歎曰：「晉以子敬、季琰為此職，今以王延之、張緒為之，可謂清官。

translations.literal: He Dian sighed and said, “Jin appointed Wang Xianzhi and Gu Hui to these posts; now Wang Yanzhi and Zhang Xu hold them—one may call these pure offices.
translations.idiomatic: He Dian sighed, “Jin gave these posts to Wang Xianzhi and Gu Hui; now Wang Yanzhi and Zhang Xu hold them—true pure offices.

sentences.zh: 後接之者，實為未易。

translations.literal: Those who follow will truly not find it easy.
translations.idiomatic: Successors will have a hard act to follow.

sentences.zh: 」緒長於周易，言精理奧，見宗一時。

translations.literal: ” Xu was expert in the Book of Changes; his words were refined in principle and profound, and he was honored for a time.
translations.idiomatic: Expert in the Book of Changes, his discourse was subtle and commanded the age.

sentences.zh: 常云：「何平叔不解易中七事」。

translations.literal: He often said, “He Pingshu did not understand seven matters in the Changes.”
translations.idiomatic: He often said He Yan never grasped seven points in the Changes.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，轉吏部尚書，祭酒如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu acceded, Xu was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel while retaining his post as Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he became director of personnel while keeping the university directorship.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，領南郡王師，加給事中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he served as Tutor to Prince of Nan Commandery with the added title Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 2 he tutored Prince of Nan Commandery as attendant.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉太子詹事，師、給事如故。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, retaining tutor and attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 緒每朝見，武帝目送之，謂王儉曰：「緒以位尊我，我以德貴緒。

translations.literal: Whenever Xu attended audience, Emperor Wu watched him depart and said to Wang Jian, “Xu honors me by rank; I honor Xu by virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At court audiences the emperor watched Xu leave and told Wang Jian, “He outranks me in office; I outrank him in virtue.

sentences.zh: 」遷散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，師如故，給親信二十人。

translations.literal: ” He was transferred to Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, tutor as before, with twenty personal attendants.
translations.idiomatic: ” Promoted to regular attendant and grand master with golden seal, he kept twenty personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 復領中正。

translations.literal: He again headed the grand arbiter’s office.
translations.idiomatic: He again headed grand arbiter appointments.

sentences.zh: 長沙王晃屬選用吳郡聞人邕為州議曹，緒以資籍不當，執不許。

translations.literal: Prince of Changsha Huang wished to appoint Wenren Yong of Wu Commandery as provincial selection officer; Xu, because Yong’s pedigree was unsuitable, firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changsha Huang wanted Wenren Yong as provincial selection officer; Xu refused on grounds of pedigree.

sentences.zh: 晃遺書於緒固請之，緒正色謂晃信曰：「此是身家州鄉，殿下何得見逼。

translations.literal: Huang sent a letter pressing the matter; Xu sternly told Huang’s messenger, “This man is from my home commandery—how can Your Highness coerce me?
translations.idiomatic: Huang pressed by letter; Xu told the messenger, “He is from my own commandery—Your Highness cannot bully me into this.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: ” The matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ” The appointment stopped.

sentences.zh: 緒吐納風流，聽者皆忘饑疲，見者肅然如在宗廟。

translations.literal: Xu’s discourse flowed with grace; listeners forgot hunger and fatigue, and those who saw him felt solemn as if in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: His conversation was so graceful that listeners forgot weariness and onlookers stood as if in temple rites.

sentences.zh: 雖終日與居，莫能測焉。

translations.literal: Though one sat with him all day, none could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Even daily companions could not plumb him.

sentences.zh: 劉悛之為益州，獻蜀柳數株，枝條甚長，狀若絲縷。

translations.literal: When Liu Yan was in Yi Province he presented several willow trees from Shu; the branches were very long and shaped like silk threads.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, governing Yi Province, sent several Shu willows with long threadlike branches.

sentences.zh: 時舊宮芳林苑始成，武帝以植於太昌靈和殿前，常賞玩咨嗟，曰：「此楊柳風流可愛，似張緒當年時。

translations.literal: At that time the old palace’s Fanglin Garden had just been completed; Emperor Wu planted them before the Hall of Grand Brilliance and often admired them, saying, “These willows are charmingly graceful, like Zhang Xu in his prime.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planted them before the Hall of Grand Brilliance and said, “These graceful willows remind me of Zhang Xu in his prime.

sentences.zh: 」其見賞愛如此。

translations.literal: ” Such was the affection in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor cherished him to that degree.

sentences.zh: 王儉為尚書令、丹陽尹，時諸令史來問訊，有一令史善俯仰，進止可觀。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was Director of the Secretariat and Governor of Danyang; when the chief clerks came to pay their respects, one clerk’s bows and movements were notably graceful.
translations.idiomatic: As director and Danyang governor, Wang Jian noticed one clerk’s graceful bows among those paying respects.

sentences.zh: 儉賞異之，問曰：「經與誰共事？

translations.literal: Jian admired him and asked, “With whom did you study office?
translations.idiomatic: Jian asked, “Under whom did you learn deportment?

sentences.zh: 」答云：「十餘歲在張令門下。

translations.literal: ” He answered, “For more than ten years I served under Magistrate Zhang.”
translations.idiomatic: ” He answered, “More than ten years under Magistrate Zhang.”

sentences.zh: 」儉目送之。

translations.literal: ” Jian watched him depart.
translations.idiomatic: Jian watched him go.

sentences.zh: 時尹丞殷存至在坐，曰：「是康成門人也。」

translations.literal: Assistant Magistrate Yin Cunzhi was present and said, “He is a disciple of Kangcheng.”
translations.idiomatic: Assistant magistrate Yin Cunzhi said, “A disciple of Kangcheng—that is, Zhang Xu.”

sentences.zh: 七年，竟陵王子良領國子祭酒，武帝敕王晏曰：「吾欲令司徒辭祭酒以授張緒，物議以為如何？

translations.literal: In the seventh year Prince of Jingling Ziliang held the post of Director of the National University; Emperor Wu ordered Wang Yan, “I wish to have the Minister of Ceremonies resign the directorship and give it to Zhang Xu—what does public opinion think?
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Emperor Wu asked Wang Yan whether Zhang Xu should replace Prince of Jingling Ziliang as university director.

sentences.zh: 」子良竟不拜，以緒領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: ” Ziliang in the end did not accept the appointment, and Xu took charge of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang declined; Xu took the university.

sentences.zh: 緒口不言利，有財輒散之。

translations.literal: Xu never spoke of profit; whenever he had wealth he gave it away.
translations.idiomatic: He never spoke of gain and gave away whatever wealth came to hand.

sentences.zh: 清談端坐，或竟日無食。

translations.literal: He would sit in pure conversation upright, sometimes for a whole day without eating.
translations.idiomatic: He might spend a whole day in pure talk without eating.

sentences.zh: 門生見緒饑，為之辦餐，然未嘗求也。

translations.literal: When his students saw Xu hungry they would prepare food for him, yet he never asked.
translations.idiomatic: Students sometimes brought him food when he went hungry, though he never asked.

sentences.zh: 死之日，無宅以殯，遺命「凶事不設柳翣，止以蘆葭。

translations.literal: On the day of his death he had no house for the coffin; his testament read, “For mourning do not set up willow fans—only reeds and rushes.
translations.idiomatic: He died without a house for burial; his will said, “No willow fans at mourning—only reeds and rushes.

sentences.zh: 車需車引柩，靈上置杯水香火，不設祭」。

translations.literal: The cart needs only oxen to draw the bier; on the spirit seat place a cup of water and incense—do not set out offerings.”
translations.idiomatic: An ox cart for the bier; a cup of water and incense on the spirit seat—no offerings.”

sentences.zh: 從弟融敬緒，事之如親兄。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Rong revered Xu and served him like an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Rong revered him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 齎酒於緒靈前酌飲慟哭曰：「阿兄風流頓盡。

translations.literal: He brought wine before Xu’s spirit, poured and drank, and wailed, “Elder brother, your grace is utterly gone.
translations.idiomatic: At Xu’s bier Rong poured wine and wailed, “Brother, your grace is gone.

sentences.zh: 」追贈散騎常侍、特進、光祿大夫，諡簡子。

translations.literal: ” He was posthumously given Regular Attendant, Special Advance, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; his posthumous title was Jianzi.
translations.idiomatic: ” Posthumously he received regular attendant, special advance, and grand master of splendid happiness, titled Jianzi.

sentences.zh: 子完，宋後廢帝時為正員郎，險行見寵，坐廢錮。

translations.literal: His son Wan, during the reign of the deposed emperor of Song, was a regular lang; his reckless conduct won favor and he was confined by edict.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wan, a regular lang under the deposed Song emperor, was confined for debauchery that had won favor at court.

sentences.zh: 完弟允，永明中安西功曹，淫通殺人伏法。

translations.literal: Wan’s younger brother Yun, an merit officer on the western staff in Yongming, was executed for adultery and murder.
translations.idiomatic: Wan’s brother Yun, a western staff officer in Yongming, was executed for adultery and murder.

sentences.zh: 允兄充知名。

translations.literal: Yun’s elder brother Chong was well known.
translations.idiomatic: Yun’s elder brother Chong was celebrated.

sentences.zh: 演子 充

translations.literal: Yan’s son: Chong
translations.idiomatic: Yan’s son: Chong

sentences.zh: 充字延符，少好逸遊。

translations.literal: Chong, styled Yanfu, from youth loved roaming and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, styled Yanfu, loved pleasure and wandering from youth.

sentences.zh: 緒嘗告歸至吳，始入西郭，逢充獵，右臂鷹，左牽狗。

translations.literal: When Xu was returning home to Wu, just entering the western suburb he met Chong hunting, hawk on right arm and dog in left hand.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, returning to Wu, met Chong in the western suburbs hunting with hawk and hound.

sentences.zh: 遇緒船至，便放絏脫鞋拜于水次。

translations.literal: Seeing Xu’s boat arrive, Chong at once released the leash, removed his shoes, and bowed at the water’s edge.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Xu’s boat, Chong loosed his hawk, shed his shoes, and bowed at the shore.

sentences.zh: 緒曰：「一身兩役，無乃勞乎。

translations.literal: Xu said, “One body serving two tasks—is it not too much labor?
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, “One body, two occupations—is that not too much?

sentences.zh: 」充跪曰：「充聞三十而立，今充二十九矣，請至來歲。

translations.literal: ” Chong knelt and said, “I have heard that at thirty one stands firm; I am now twenty-nine—please grant me until next year.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chong knelt: “They say a man stands firm at thirty; I am twenty-nine—give me one year.

sentences.zh: 」緒曰：「過而能改，顏氏子有焉。

translations.literal: ” Xu said, “To err and reform—there is something of the disciple of Yan in this.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xu said, “To reform after fault—that is worthy of Yan Hui.

sentences.zh: 」及明年便修改，多所該通，尤明老、易，能清言。

translations.literal: ” The next year he indeed reformed; he became broadly learned, especially in the Laozi and Changes, and could engage in pure talk.
translations.idiomatic: ” The next year he reformed, mastered the Laozi and Changes, and excelled at pure talk.

sentences.zh: 與從叔稷俱有令譽。

translations.literal: He and his younger cousin Ji both enjoyed fine repute.
translations.idiomatic: He and his cousin Ji shared a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 曆尚書殿中郎、武陵王友。

translations.literal: He successively served as Lang in the Palace Section of the Ministry and Friend to Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He served as palace-section lang and friend to Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令王儉當朝用事，齊武帝皆取決焉。

translations.literal: At that time Director of the Secretariat Wang Jian held power in the court, and Emperor Wu of Qi decided everything through him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian then dominated court decisions for Emperor Wu of Qi.

sentences.zh: 儉方聚親賓，充縠巾葛帔，至便求酒，言論放逸，一坐盡傾。

translations.literal: Jian was gathering kin and guests when Chong came in a gauze headcloth and hemp sash, at once asked for wine, and spoke with abandon—the whole gathering was captivated.
translations.idiomatic: At a gathering of kin and guests Chong arrived in rustic dress, demanded wine, and talked with such abandon that the room was enthralled.

sentences.zh: 及聞武帝欲以緒為尚書僕射，儉執不可。

translations.literal: When he heard the Emperor wished to make Xu Director of the Secretariat, Jian firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the emperor wanted Xu as vice director, Jian blocked it.

sentences.zh: 充以為慍，與儉書曰：

translations.literal: Chong took this as resentment and wrote Jian a letter:
translations.idiomatic: Angered, Chong wrote Jian:

sentences.zh: 頃日路長，霖霞韜晦，敘暑未平，想無虧攝。

translations.literal: Of late the road has been long, mist and rain have hidden the light, and the lingering heat is not yet settled—I trust you have not suffered in health.
translations.idiomatic: Lately roads are long, rains have dimmed the sky, and summer heat lingers—I trust you are well.

sentences.zh: 充幸以漁釣之閑，鎌采之暇，時復引軸以自娛，逍遙乎前史。

translations.literal: Chong, fortunate in the leisure of fishing and the spare moments of reaping, sometimes unrolls scrolls for amusement and wanders freely through former histories.
translations.idiomatic: In fishing idleness and harvest spare hours I sometimes read old histories for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 從橫萬古，動默之路多端，紛綸百年，升降之塗不一。

translations.literal: Stretching across ten thousand ages, the paths of action and stillness are many; tangled through a hundred years, the roads of rise and fall are not one.
translations.idiomatic: Across ten thousand years paths of action diverge; through centuries roads of rise and fall differ.

sentences.zh: 故金剛水柔，性之別也；

translations.literal: Thus the diamond is hard and water is soft—the natures differ;
translations.idiomatic: Diamond is hard, water soft—natures differ;

sentences.zh: 圓行方止，器之異也。

translations.literal: the circle moves and the square stops—the vessels differ.
translations.idiomatic: circles roll, squares halt—vessels differ.

sentences.zh: 善禦性者，不違金水之質；

translations.literal: One who is good at mastering nature does not violate the quality of metal and water;
translations.idiomatic: Those who master nature do not fight metal or water;

sentences.zh: 善為器者，不易方圓之用。

translations.literal: one who is good at making vessels does not change the use of square and circle.
translations.idiomatic: those who craft vessels do not force square and circle against their use.

sentences.zh: 充生平少偶，不以利欲幹懷，三十六年，差得以棲貧自澹。

translations.literal: In all my life Chong has rarely found a match; profit and desire do not touch his heart—for thirty-six years he has barely managed to dwell in poverty with contentment.
translations.idiomatic: I have rarely met my equal; gain does not touch me—for thirty-six years I have lived poor and content.

sentences.zh: 介然之志，峭聳霜崖，確乎之情，峰橫海岸。

translations.literal: His detached will rises steep as frost cliffs; his firm feeling stands peak-like above the sea.
translations.idiomatic: My resolve rises like frost cliffs; my loyalty stands like peaks above the sea.

sentences.zh: 至如彯纓天閣，既謝廊廟之華，綴組雲台，終愧衣冠之秀。

translations.literal: As for dangling tassels at the heavenly gate, he has already declined the glory of court and hall; linking seals on the cloud terrace, he ends by ashamed before the elegance of cap and robe.
translations.idiomatic: Court tassels at the heavenly gate I have refused; cloud-terrace seals I would wear with shame.

sentences.zh: 實由氣岸疏凝，情塗狷隔。

translations.literal: Truly because his spirit-shores are sparse and congealed and the paths of feeling are narrow and blocked.
translations.idiomatic: My spirit stands apart; feeling’s paths are blocked.

sentences.zh: 獨師懷抱，不見許於俗人，孤秀神崖，每邅回於在世。

translations.literal: He follows only his own bosom, not granted approval by vulgar men; a lone peak of spirit, always turning back in this world.
translations.idiomatic: I follow my own heart, unapproved by the crowd, a lone peak always turning back from the world.

sentences.zh: 長群魚鳥，畢景松阿。

translations.literal: Long he herds fish and birds, ending his days among pines.
translations.idiomatic: I herd fish and birds and end my days among pines.

sentences.zh: 雖復玉沒於訪珪之辰，桂掩於搜芳之日，氾濫于漁父之游，偃息于卜居之會，如此而已，充何識哉。

translations.literal: Though jade is lost in the hour of seeking gems and cassia hidden in the day of gathering fragrance, wandering in the fisherman’s roam and resting in the diviner’s meeting—so much and no more; what does Chong know?
translations.idiomatic: Though gems are lost and fragrance missed, I wander like a fisherman and rest like a diviner—that is all I know.

sentences.zh: 若夫驚岩罩日，吐海逢天，竦石崩尋，分危落仞。

translations.literal: If one speaks of cliffs that startle and cover the sun, seas that spew and meet the sky, towering stones collapsing in fathoms, split peril falling from thousand- ren heights.
translations.idiomatic: Think of cliffs that blot the sun, seas that meet the sky, stones crashing from thousand-ren heights.

sentences.zh: 桂蘭綺靡，叢雜於山幽，松柏陰森，相繚於澗側。

translations.literal: Osmanthus and orchids luxuriant, tangled in mountain depths; pines and cypresses dark and dense, winding along stream banks.
translations.idiomatic: Orchids tangle in deep mountains; cypress shade lines the streams.

sentences.zh: 元卿於是乎不歸，伯休亦以茲長往。

translations.literal: Lord Yuan then did not return; Lord Bo also for this reason departed forever.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yuan never returned; Lord Bo left forever for such scenes.

sentences.zh: 至於飛竿釣渚，濯足滄洲，獨浪煙霞，高臥風月，悠悠琴酒，岫遠誰來，灼灼文言，空擬方寸。

translations.literal: As for casting rods on islets, washing feet in blue waters, alone riding mist and rosy clouds, lying high in wind and moon, distant lute and wine—who comes from the peaks? Blazing letters—empty against the inch of the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Rods on islets, feet in blue waters, alone in mist and moon—distant music, blazing letters, none to share the heart’s inch.

sentences.zh: 不覺郁然千里，路隔江川，每至西風，何嘗不歎。

translations.literal: Unawares gloom stretches a thousand li, roads blocked by rivers; whenever the west wind rises, how can one not sigh?
translations.idiomatic: Gloom stretches a thousand li; rivers block the way—when the west wind rises, who does not sigh?

sentences.zh: 丈人歲路未強，學優而仕，道佐蒼生，功橫海望，可謂德盛當時，孤松獨秀者也。

translations.literal: Sir, your years’ road is not yet strong; learning is excellent and you serve in office; your Way assists the blue-gowned people and your merit spans the sea’s horizon—you may be called virtuous flourishing in the age, a lone pine standing in excellence.
translations.idiomatic: You are not yet old, learned and in office, aiding the people with merit spanning the seas—a virtuous pine standing alone in the age.

sentences.zh: 而茂陵之彥，望冠蓋而長懷，渭川之甿，佇簪裾而竦歎，得無惜乎。

translations.literal: Yet the worthy of Maoling long gaze at passing carriages and caps; the common folk of Wei River wait for sash and hem and sigh in awe—is there not regret?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Maoling’s worthies long for court processions; Wei River folk wait for official dress—is there no regret?

sentences.zh: 充昆西百姓，岱表一人，蠶而衣，耕而食。

translations.literal: Chong is a common man west of the Kun, one man on Dai’s frontier—silkworms for clothing, plow for food.
translations.idiomatic: I am a common man west of Kun, one man on the frontier—silkworms for clothes, plow for food.

sentences.zh: 不能事王侯，覓知己，造時人，騁遊說。

translations.literal: He cannot serve lords and princes, seek confidants, court men of the age, or roam in persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot serve lords, seek patrons, court the powerful, or roam as persuader.

sentences.zh: 容與于屠博之間，其歡甚矣。

translations.literal: He wanders content among butchers and gamblers; his joy is very great.
translations.idiomatic: I am content among butchers and gamblers—that joy is enough.

sentences.zh: 然舉世皆謂充為狂，充亦何能與諸君道之哉。

translations.literal: Yet the whole world calls Chong mad; how can Chong discuss this with you gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: The world calls me mad; how could I explain that to you?

sentences.zh: 是以披聞見，掃心胸，述平生，論語默。

translations.literal: Therefore he spreads what he has heard, sweeps the heart and breast, narrates his life, and discusses speech and silence.
translations.idiomatic: So I lay open my heart, tell my life, and speak of word and silence.

sentences.zh: 所可通夢交魂、推襟送抱者，唯丈人而已。

translations.literal: Those with whom one may connect in dream and soul, push lapels and embrace, is only you, sir.
translations.idiomatic: Only with you, sir, can I join souls and embrace as kin.

sentences.zh: 闕廷敻阻，書罷莫因，儻遇樵夫，妄塵執事。

translations.literal: Court and audience are far apart; when the letter ends there is no means to send it—if by chance a woodcutter passes, forgive the dust on your desk.
translations.idiomatic: Court is far; when this letter ends I have no courier—if a woodcutter carries it, forgive the dust on your desk.

sentences.zh: 儉以為脫略，弗之重，仍以書示緒，緒杖之一百。

translations.literal: Jian thought it unrestrained and did not value it; he still showed the letter to Xu, and Xu beat Chong with a staff a hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: Jian dismissed it as reckless but showed Xu, who caned Chong a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 又為御史中丞到撝所奏，免官禁錮。

translations.literal: He was again impeached by Censor-in-Chief Dao Hui and dismissed from office and confined.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Dao Hui impeached him; he was dismissed and confined.

sentences.zh: 沈約見其書，歎曰：「充始為之敗，終為之成。

translations.literal: When Shen Yue saw the letter he sighed and said, “Chong begins in defeat and ends in success.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue read the letter and sighed, “Chong fails at the start and triumphs at the end.

sentences.zh: 」久之，為司徒諮議參軍，與琅邪王思遠、同郡陸慧曉等並為司徒竟陵王賓客。

translations.literal: ” After a long time he became Senior Adviser on the Secretariat staff and, with Langya Wang Siyuan and fellow townsman Lu Huixiao, served together as guests of Prince of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: ” Later he advised the secretariat and joined Wang Siyuan of Langya and Lu Huixiao as guests of Prince of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 累遷義興太守，為政清靜，吏人便之。

translations.literal: He rose through the ranks to Governor of Yixing; his governance was pure and quiet, and officials and people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Yixing he ruled quietly to the people’s ease.

sentences.zh: 後為侍中。

translations.literal: Later he became Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He later became attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝兵至建鄴，東昏逢殺，百官集西鍾下，召充，充不至。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang’s army reached Jiankang, Dong Hun was killed; the hundred officials assembled beneath the western bell, but Chong was summoned and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang troops reached Jiankang and Dong Hun was killed, officials gathered at the western bell; Chong did not come.

sentences.zh: 武帝霸府建，以充為大司馬諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor’s hegemonic headquarters was established, Chong was made Senior Adviser on the Grand Marshal’s staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the hegemonic headquarters he became grand marshal adviser.

sentences.zh: 天監初，曆太常卿、吏部尚書，居選以平允稱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he successively served as Minister of Ceremonies and Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and in appointments was known for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian he headed ceremonies and personnel, famed for even-handed appointments.

sentences.zh: 再遷散騎常侍、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Regular Attendant and Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He again became regular attendant and university director.

sentences.zh: 登堂講說，皇太子以下皆至。

translations.literal: Ascending the hall to lecture, the crown prince and all below came.
translations.idiomatic: When he lectured, the crown prince and court attended.

sentences.zh: 時王侯多在學，執經以拜，充朝服而立，不敢當。

translations.literal: At that time princes and nobles were mostly in the university; holding the classics they bowed, and Chong stood in court dress and did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: Princes in the university bowed over the classics; Chong stood in court dress and refused the honor.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書僕射。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose again to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as Governor of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent to govern Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 下車恤貧老，故舊莫不忻悅。

translations.literal: On taking office he cared for the poor and elderly; old friends all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Taking office he succored the poor and elderly; old friends rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 卒于吳郡，諡曰穆子。

translations.literal: He died in Wu Commandery; his posthumous title was Muzi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Wu Commandery and was titled Muzi.

sentences.zh: 子最嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zui succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 永子 瑰

translations.literal: Yong’s son: Gui
translations.idiomatic: Yong’s son: Gui

sentences.zh: 瑰字祖逸，宋征北將軍、南兗州刺史永之子也。

translations.literal: Gui, styled Zuyi, was the son of Yong, General Who Conquers the North and Governor of Southern Yan in Song.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, styled Zuyi, was son of Yong, Song’s northern general and governor of southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 仕宋，累遷桂陽內史。

translations.literal: He served in Song and rose through the ranks to Internal Administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song he rose to internal administrator of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 不欲前兄瑋處祿，自免不拜。

translations.literal: He did not wish to hold salary before his elder brother Wei and resigned without accepting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to take office before elder brother Wei, he declined appointment.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒右長史，通直散騎常侍，驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Later he became Senior Aide of the Right in the Secretariat, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, and General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as right senior aide, regular attendant, and general of valiant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 出為吳興太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to govern Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 瑰以既有國秩，不取郡奉。

translations.literal: Gui, because he already held a state stipend, did not take the commandery salary.
translations.idiomatic: Already drawing a state stipend, he refused the commandery salary.

sentences.zh: 高帝敕上庫別藏其奉，以表其清。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the upper treasury to store his salary separately to display his purity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had his salary stored separately in the treasury to honor his integrity.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，為甯蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu acceded, Gui became Colonel Who Pacifies the Man and Governor of Yong Province with the added title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he pacified the Man as colonel and governed Yong with area command.

sentences.zh: 徵拜左戶尚書，加右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Director of the Left Household Ministry with the added rank of Right Army General.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he became director of the left household ministry and right army general.

sentences.zh: 還後，安陸王紆臨雍州，行部登蔓山，有野老來乞。

translations.literal: After returning, when Prince of Anlu Shu toured Yong Province and ascended Manshan on inspection, an old commoner came to beg.
translations.idiomatic: After returning, Prince of Anlu Shu toured Yong and climbed Manshan; an old man came begging.

sentences.zh: 紆問：「何不事產而行乞邪？

translations.literal: Shu asked, “Why do you not work a livelihood and instead go begging?
translations.idiomatic: Shu asked, “Why beg instead of working?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「張使君臨州理物，百姓家得相保。

translations.literal: ” He answered, “When Commissioner Zhang governed the province and ordered affairs, common people’s households could protect one another.
translations.idiomatic: ” He answered, “When Commissioner Zhang governed, families could protect themselves.

sentences.zh: 後人政嚴，故至行乞。

translations.literal: Later men’s governance was strict, and so I have come to beg.
translations.idiomatic: Later governors were harsh, so I beg now.

sentences.zh: 」紆由是深加嗟賞。

translations.literal: ” Shu therefore deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shu sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 後拜太常，自謂閒職，輒歸家。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies; he considered it an idle post and at once returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Made minister of ceremonies, he deemed it idle and went home at once.

sentences.zh: 武帝曰：「卿輩未富貴，謂人不與；

translations.literal: The Emperor said, “You gentlemen are not yet wealthy and think people will not give you office;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “When you were poor you thought the world would not employ you;

sentences.zh: 既富貴，那復欲委去。

translations.literal: once wealthy, why again wish to cast it off?
translations.idiomatic: now wealthy, why throw office away?

sentences.zh: 」瑰曰：「陛下禦臣等若養馬，無事就閑廄，有事復牽來。

translations.literal: ” Gui said, “Your Majesty tends us ministers like raising horses—when idle we go to the stable, when needed we are led out again.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gui replied, “Your Majesty keeps us like horses—idle in the stable, led out when needed.

sentences.zh: 」帝猶怒，遂以為散騎常侍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor was still angry and therefore made him Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: ” Angered, the emperor made him regular attendant and grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 郁林之廢，朝臣到宮門參承明帝。

translations.literal: At the deposition of Prince of Yulin, court ministers went to the palace gate to pay respects to Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yulin was deposed, ministers waited at the palace gate for Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 瑰托腳疾不至。

translations.literal: Gui pleaded foot ailment and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Gui pleaded foot ailment and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 海陵立，明帝疑外藩起兵，以瑰鎮石頭，督眾軍事。

translations.literal: When Prince of Hailing acceded, Emperor Ming feared rebellion in outer provinces and made Gui guard Shitou with command over all armies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, fearing frontier rebellion, put Gui in command at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 瑰見朝廷多難，遂恒臥疾。

translations.literal: Gui saw the court beset with difficulties and therefore constantly feigned illness.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing turmoil at court, Gui feigned chronic illness.

sentences.zh: 建武末，屢啟求還吳，見許。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianwu he repeatedly memorialized asking to return to Wu and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianwu he repeatedly asked to return to Wu and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 居室豪富，伎妾盈房。

translations.literal: His residence was lavishly rich and his concubines filled the rooms.
translations.idiomatic: His house was lavish and concubines filled the chambers.

sentences.zh: 或者譏其衰暮畜伎。

translations.literal: Some ridiculed him for keeping entertainers in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Some mocked him for keeping entertainers in old age.

sentences.zh: 瑰曰：「我少好音律，老而方解。

translations.literal: Gui said, “From youth I loved music; only in old age do I understand it.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, “I loved music young and only now in age understand it.

sentences.zh: 平生嗜欲，無復一存，唯未能遣此耳。」

translations.literal: In all my life’s desires nothing else remains; I simply cannot part with this.”
translations.idiomatic: Every other appetite is gone—I cannot give this up.”

sentences.zh: 明帝疾甚，防疑大司馬王敬則，授瑰平東將軍、吳郡太守，以為之備。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was gravely ill he guarded against Grand Marshal Wang Jingze and appointed Gui General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Wu Commandery to prepare against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gravely ill, Emperor Ming feared Wang Jingze and made Gui pacifier of the east at Wu to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 及敬則反，瑰遣兵迎拒於松江。

translations.literal: When Jingze rebelled, Gui sent troops to meet and resist him at Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingze rebelled, Gui sent troops to Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 聞敬則軍鼓聲，一時散走。

translations.literal: Hearing Jingze’s army drums, they scattered at once.
translations.idiomatic: At the sound of Jingze’s drums his men fled.

sentences.zh: 瑰棄郡逃人間，事平乃還郡，為有司奏，免官削爵。

translations.literal: Gui abandoned the commandery and fled among the people; only after the affair was settled did he return to the commandery, was reported by the relevant office, and was dismissed from office and stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the commandery and hid among commoners; after order returned he was reported, dismissed, and stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 永元初，為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongyuan he was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongyuan’s start he was grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 三年，梁武帝起兵，東昏假瑰節，戍石頭，尋棄城還宮。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops, Dong Hun lent Gui his seal to guard Shitou; soon he abandoned the city and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Liang troops rose; Dong Hun lent Gui his seal to hold Shitou, then he abandoned the city.

sentences.zh: 梁天監元年，拜給事中、右光祿大夫，以腳疾拜於家。

translations.literal: In the first year of Liang Tianjian he was appointed Attendant and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; because of foot ailment he received appointment at home.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 1 he became attendant and right grand master; foot ailment kept him at home.

sentences.zh: 四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 瑰有子十二人，常云：「中應有好者」。

translations.literal: Gui had twelve sons and often said, “Among them there ought to be a good one.”
translations.idiomatic: With twelve sons he often said, “One of them should turn out well.”

sentences.zh: 子率知名。

translations.literal: His son Shuai was well known.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuai was celebrated.

sentences.zh: 瑰子 率

translations.literal: Gui’s son: Shuai
translations.idiomatic: Gui’s son: Shuai

sentences.zh: 率字士簡，性寬雅。

translations.literal: Shuai, styled Shijian, was by nature broad and refined.
translations.idiomatic: Shuai, styled Shijian, was open and refined by nature.

sentences.zh: 十二能屬文，常日限為詩一篇，或數日不作，則追補之，稍進作賦頌，至年十六，向作二千餘首。

translations.literal: At twelve he could compose prose; he habitually limited himself to one poem a day, or if several days passed without writing he would make up the deficit; gradually he advanced to composing fu and eulogies, and by sixteen he had written more than two thousand pieces.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he wrote prose, one poem a day by habit, making up missed days; by sixteen he had written over two thousand poems and fu.

sentences.zh: 有虞訥者見而詆之，率乃一旦焚毀，更為詩示焉，托雲沈約。

translations.literal: There was a Yu Ne who slandered him; Shuai then burned everything in one day and wrote new poems to show him, attributing them to Shen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Ne mocked his work, Shuai burned it all and showed new poems attributed to Shen Yue.

sentences.zh: 訥便句句嗟稱，無字不善。

translations.literal: Ne then praised every line and found no word unskilled.
translations.idiomatic: Ne praised every line as flawless.

sentences.zh: 率曰：「此吾作也。

translations.literal: Shuai said, “These are my compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Shuai said, “I wrote these.

sentences.zh: 」訥慚而退。

translations.literal: ” Ne withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ne withdrew ashamed.

sentences.zh: 時陸少玄家有父澄書萬餘卷，率與少玄善，遂通書籍，盡讀其書。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Shaoxuan’s family had more than ten thousand scrolls left by his father Cheng; Shuai was on good terms with Shaoxuan and thus gained access to the books and read them all.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shaoxuan owned ten thousand scrolls from his father; befriending him, Shuai read them all.

sentences.zh: 建武三年，舉秀才，除太子舍人，與同郡陸倕、陸厥幼相友狎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwu he was recommended as Outstanding Talent, appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and was from youth close friends with fellow townsman Lu Cheng and Lu Jue.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 3, recommended as outstanding talent, he became attendant of the heir apparent and befriended Lu Cheng and Lu Jue.

sentences.zh: 嘗同載詣左衛將軍沈約，遇任昉在焉。

translations.literal: They once rode together to visit Left Guard General Shen Yue; Ren Fang happened to be there.
translations.idiomatic: They once visited Shen Yue together; Ren Fang was present.

sentences.zh: 約謂昉曰：「此二子後進才秀，皆南金也，卿可識之。

translations.literal: Yue said to Fang, “These two young men are talented sprouts of the later generation—southern gold; you should know them.
translations.idiomatic: Yue told Fang, “These two are southern gold—you should know them.

sentences.zh: 」由此與昉友。

translations.literal: ” From this he became friends with Fang.
translations.idiomatic: ” Thus Shuai befriended Fang.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，為司徒謝朏掾，直文德待詔省，敕使抄乙部書，又使撰古婦人事。

translations.literal: During Liang Tianjian he was Aide to Secretariat Director Xie Tiao, awaiting orders at the Wende drafting office; he was ordered to copy the B section of books and to compile accounts of ancient women.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianjian he aided Xie Tiao, copied B-section books, and compiled accounts of ancient women.

sentences.zh: 使工書人琅邪王琛、吳郡範懷約等寫給後宮。
