translations.literal: He had scribes Wang Chen of Langya and Fan Huaiyue of Wu Commandery write copies for the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Scribes Wang Chen and Fan Huaiyue copied them for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 率取假東歸，論者謂為傲世，率懼，乃為待詔賦奏之，甚見稱賞。

translations.literal: Shuai took leave to return east; critics said he was arrogant toward the world, and Shuai, fearing this, composed a memorial fu and submitted it, winning great praise.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave east, he was called arrogant; fearing this, he submitted a memorial fu and won praise.

sentences.zh: 手敕答曰：「相如工而不敏，枚皋速而不工，卿可謂兼二子于金馬矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor answered by hand, “Sima Xiangru was skilled but not quick, Mei Gao quick but not skilled—you may be said to unite both in the Golden Horse Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied by hand, “Sima Xiangru was skilled but slow, Mei Gao fast but rough—you unite both at the Golden Horse Gate.

sentences.zh: 」又侍宴賦詩，武帝別賜率詩曰：「東南有才子，故能服官政，余雖慚古昔，得人今為盛。

translations.literal: ” At another banquet he composed poetry; the Emperor separately bestowed a poem on Shuai saying, “In the southeast there is an outstanding talent, and so he can serve in office; though I am ashamed before the ancients, in gaining men the present excels.
translations.idiomatic: At banquet the emperor gifted him a poem: “Southeast holds a talent fit for office; though I fall short of ancients, today excels in men.

sentences.zh: 」率奏詩往反六首。

translations.literal: ” Shuai submitted six poems in reply.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shuai answered with six poems.

sentences.zh: 後引見於玉衡殿，謂曰：「卿東南物望，朕宿昔所聞。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to Yuhheng Hall; the Emperor said, “Your reputation in the southeast I have long heard from of old.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to Yuhheng Hall, the emperor said, “Your southeastern fame I have long known.

sentences.zh: 卿言宰相是何人，不從天下，不由地出。

translations.literal: Tell me who the chief minister is—not from heaven, not from earth.
translations.idiomatic: Tell me who the chief minister is—neither from heaven nor earth.

sentences.zh: 卿名家奇才，若復以禮律為意，便是其人。

translations.literal: You are an outstanding talent of a famous house; if you again take ritual and law to heart, you will be the man.
translations.idiomatic: You are a great house’s talent; take ritual and law to heart and you are the man.

sentences.zh: 秘書丞天下清官，東南望胄未有為之者，今以相處，為卿定名譽。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat is the realm’s pure office; no southeastern noble heir has yet held it—now I appoint you to it to fix your reputation for you.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary director is the realm’s purest post; no southern heir has held it—I give it to you to seal your name.

sentences.zh: 」尋以為秘書丞，掌集書詔策。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Director of the Secretariat, in charge of collecting edicts and memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became secretary director, collecting edicts and memorials.

sentences.zh: 四年，禊飲華光殿，其日河南國獻赤龍駒，能拜伏，善舞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, at the spring purification feast in Huaguang Hall, that day Henan State presented a crimson dragon colt that could bow and prostrate and dance well.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year at Huaguang Hall’s spring feast, Henan presented a crimson dragon colt that bowed and danced.

sentences.zh: 詔率與到溉、周興嗣為賦，武帝以率及興嗣為工。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shuai, Dao Gai, and Zhou Xingsi to compose fu; the Emperor judged Shuai and Xingsi superior.
translations.idiomatic: Shuai, Dao Gai, and Zhou Xingsi were ordered to compose fu; the emperor favored Shuai and Xingsi.

sentences.zh: 其年，父憂去職。

translations.literal: That year he left office for mourning his father.
translations.idiomatic: That year he left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 有父時妓數十人，其善謳者有色貌，邑子儀曹郎顧珖之求娉，謳者不願，遂出家為尼。

translations.literal: There were several dozen of his father’s former entertainers; among the skilled singers one had beauty and appearance; the district gentleman Gu Gongzhi of the Ceremonies Section sought to marry her, but the singer was unwilling and became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: His father’s dozens of singers included a beautiful skilled one; Gu Gongzhi sought to marry her, but she became a nun instead.

sentences.zh: 嘗因齋會率宅，珖之乃飛書言與率奸。

translations.literal: Once during a fast at Shuai’s house, Gongzhi sent a flying letter accusing Shuai of adultery with her.
translations.idiomatic: During a fast at Shuai’s house Gongzhi sent a letter accusing Shuai of adultery with her.

sentences.zh: 南司以事奏聞，武帝惜其才，寢其奏，然猶致時論。

translations.literal: The Southern Bureau reported the matter; the Emperor valued his talent and suppressed the memorial, yet public opinion still arose.
translations.idiomatic: The southern bureau reported it; the emperor suppressed the charge but gossip remained.

sentences.zh: 服闋，久之不仕。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he long did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he long refused office.

sentences.zh: 七年，除中權建安王中記室參軍，俄直壽光省，修丙丁部書抄。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Senior Recorder on Prince of Jian’an’s staff, then soon served at the Shouguang office copying the C and D sections of books.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he recorded for Prince of Jian’an, then copied C- and D-section books at Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 累遷晉安王宣惠諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He rose through the ranks to Senior Adviser to Prince of Jin’an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to senior adviser to Prince of Jin’an.

sentences.zh: 率在府十年，恩禮甚篤。

translations.literal: Shuai was at the princely residence for ten years and received very generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years at the princely residence brought generous favor.

sentences.zh: 後為揚州別駕。

translations.literal: Later he became Vice Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later became vice governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 率雖曆居職務，未嘗留心簿領。

translations.literal: Though Shuai held office successively, he never applied his mind to registers and documents.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held many posts, he never minded ledgers.

sentences.zh: 及為別駕奏事，武帝覽牒問之，並無對，但答云：「事在牒中。

translations.literal: When as Vice Governor he submitted business, the Emperor read the documents and questioned him; he had no answers and only replied, “The matter is in the document.
translations.idiomatic: As vice governor he submitted business; questioned by the emperor, he answered only, “It is in the document.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 後曆黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 出為新安太守，丁所生母憂卒。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Xin’an; while in mourning for his birth mother he died.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Xin’an, he died mourning his birth mother.

sentences.zh: 率嗜酒不事，于家務尤忘懷。

translations.literal: Shuai loved wine and did not attend to affairs; in household matters he was especially forgetful.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and neglected affairs, especially at home.

sentences.zh: 在新安遣家僮載米三千石還宅，及至遂耗太半。

translations.literal: While in Xin’an he sent a household servant to carry three thousand shi of rice home; when it arrived more than half was gone.
translations.idiomatic: From Xin’an he sent three thousand shi of rice home; more than half vanished en route.

sentences.zh: 率問其故，答曰：「雀鼠耗。

translations.literal: Shuai asked the reason; the answer was, “Sparrows and rats consumed it.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, the servant said sparrows and rats ate it.

sentences.zh: 」率笑而言曰：「壯哉雀鼠。

translations.literal: ” Shuai laughed and said, “Magnificent sparrows and rats.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shuai laughed, “Magnificent sparrows and rats.

sentences.zh: 」竟不研問。

translations.literal: ” In the end he did not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: ” He never investigated.

sentences.zh: 自少屬文，七略及藝文志所載詩賦，今亡其文者，並補作之。

translations.literal: From youth he composed prose; for poetry and fu recorded in the Seven Summaries and Bibliographic Treatise whose texts are now lost, he all supplemented and wrote them.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he wrote prose; he reconstructed every lost poem and fu listed in the Seven Summaries and Bibliographic Treatise.

sentences.zh: 所著文衡十五卷，文集四十卷行於世。

translations.literal: His Literary Balance in fifteen scrolls and collected works in forty scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Literary Balance in fifteen scrolls and forty scrolls of collected works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子長公。

translations.literal: His son Changgong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changgong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 率弟盾。

translations.literal: Shuai’s younger brother Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Shuai’s younger brother Dun.

sentences.zh: 率弟 盾

translations.literal: Shuai’s younger brother: Dun
translations.idiomatic: Shuai’s younger brother: Dun

sentences.zh: 盾字士宣，以謹重稱。

translations.literal: Dun, styled Shixuan, was known for prudence and gravity.
translations.idiomatic: Dun, styled Shixuan, was known for sober prudence.

sentences.zh: 為無錫令，遇劫，問劫何須，劫以刀斫其頰，盾曰：「咄，咄，不易。

translations.literal: While Magistrate of Wuxi he met robbers; when the robbers asked what they needed, Dun had his cheek cut with a knife and said, “Tut, tut—not easy.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Wuxi he was robbed; when asked his needs, Dun let a knife cut his cheek and said, “Tut—not easy.

sentences.zh: 」餘無所言。

translations.literal: ” Beyond that he said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: ” He said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 於是生資皆盡，不以介懷。

translations.literal: Thereupon all his possessions were taken, yet he did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: They took everything; he did not care.

sentences.zh: 為湘東王記室，出監富陽令。

translations.literal: He was Recorder to Prince of Xiangdong and sent out to supervise Magistrate of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He recorded for Prince of Xiangdong and supervised Fuyang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 廓然獨處，無所用心。

translations.literal: He lived withdrawn and alone, with nothing on his mind.
translations.idiomatic: He lived withdrawn, minding nothing.

sentences.zh: 身死之日，家無遺財，唯有文集並書千餘卷，酒米數甕而已。

translations.literal: On the day of his death his house had no remaining wealth—only collected works and more than a thousand scrolls of books, plus a few jars of wine and rice.
translations.idiomatic: He died with no wealth but collected works, a thousand books, and a few jars of wine and rice.

sentences.zh: 瑰弟 稷

translations.literal: Gui’s younger brother: Ji
translations.idiomatic: Gui’s younger brother: Ji

sentences.zh: 稷字公喬，瑰弟也。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Gongqiao, was Gui’s younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Gongqiao was Gui’s younger brother.

sentences.zh: 幼有孝性，所生母劉無寵，遘疾。

translations.literal: From youth he had filial nature; his birth mother Liu was without favor and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Filial from youth, he nursed his un favored birth mother Liu when she fell ill.

sentences.zh: 時稷年十一，侍養衣不解帶，每劇則累夜不寢。

translations.literal: At that time Ji was eleven; he attended her nursing without undoing his belt, and whenever the illness grew severe he would for many nights not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he nursed her without loosening his belt and went sleepless in crises.

sentences.zh: 及終，毀瘠過人，杖而後起。

translations.literal: When she died his emaciation exceeded others’; he rose only with a staff’s support.
translations.idiomatic: At her death he wasted away and rose only with a staff.

sentences.zh: 見年輩幼童，輒哽咽泣淚，州裏謂之淳孝。

translations.literal: Seeing younger boys of his age he would choke and weep; the district called this pure filiality.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing boys his age he wept; the district called it pure filiality.

sentences.zh: 長兄瑋善彈箏，稷以劉氏先執此伎，聞瑋為清調，便悲感頓絕，遂終身不聽之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Wei was skilled at plucking the zheng; because the Liu clan had first practiced this art, when Ji heard Wei play in the clear mode he was suddenly overcome with grief and fainted, and thereafter never listened to it all his life.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Wei played zheng; hearing the Liu clan’s clear mode, Ji fainted with grief and never listened again.

sentences.zh: 性疏率，朗悟有才略，起家著作佐郎，不拜。

translations.literal: By nature he was careless and open, bright and talented with strategy; he began his career as Assistant in the Composition Office and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Careless but brilliant, he declined his first appointment as composition assistant.

sentences.zh: 父永及嫡母丘相繼殂，六年廬於墓側。

translations.literal: After his father Yong and principal mother Qiu died in succession, he dwelt in a hut by the tomb for six years.
translations.idiomatic: When father Yong and stepmother Qiu died, he mourned in a tomb hut six years.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，為豫章王嶷主簿，與彭城劉繪俱見禮接，未嘗被呼名，每呼為劉四、張五。

translations.literal: During Yongming in Qi he was Chief Clerk to Prince of Yuzhang Liao and, together with Pengcheng Liu Hui, was treated with courtesy—they were never called by name, only “Liu Four” and “Zhang Five.”
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi Yongming he served Prince of Yuzhang Liao with Liu Hui, called only “Liu Four” and “Zhang Five.”

sentences.zh: 以貧求為剡令，略不視事，多為小山遊。

translations.literal: Because he was poor he sought to be Magistrate of Shan; he scarcely looked to official business and often wandered on small mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he took magistracy of Shan, neglecting desk work for mountain walks.

sentences.zh: 會山賊唐宇之作亂，稷率厲部人保全縣境。

translations.literal: When mountain bandits Tang Yuzhi rebelled, Ji led and encouraged his district men to preserve the county territory.
translations.idiomatic: When bandit Tang Yuzhi rebelled, Ji rallied the county to defend it.

sentences.zh: 所生母劉先假葬琅邪黃山，建武中改申葬禮，賻助委積。

translations.literal: His birth mother Liu had first been provisionally buried at Mount Huang in Langya; in Jianwu the burial rites were revised and subsidies piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Birth mother Liu lay provisionally at Mount Huang; revised Jianwu rites brought piled subsidies.

sentences.zh: 于時雖不拒絕，事畢隨以還之。

translations.literal: At the time though he did not refuse, when the affair ended he at once returned everything.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted nothing permanently and returned all when done.

sentences.zh: 自幼及長，數十年中，常設劉氏神座。

translations.literal: From childhood through adulthood, for several decades he constantly set up Liu’s spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: For decades he kept Liu’s spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 出告反面，如事生焉。

translations.literal: Going out and returning he turned his face as if she were alive.
translations.idiomatic: Going out and in he treated her as living.

sentences.zh: 曆給事中黃門侍郎，新興、永甯二郡太守。

translations.literal: He successively served as Attendant, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and Governor of Xinxing and Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant, gentleman of the yellow gate, and governor of Xinxing and Yongning.

sentences.zh: 郡犯私諱，改永寧為長寧。

translations.literal: The commandery violated his personal taboo name, so Yongning was changed to Changning.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning was renamed Changning to avoid his taboo.

sentences.zh: 永元末，為侍中，宿衛宮城。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan he was Attendant and guarded the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongyuan’s end he guarded the palace as attendant.

sentences.zh: 梁武師至，兼衛尉江淹出奔，稷兼衛尉卿，副王瑩都督城內諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Liang Wu’s army arrived, Concurrent Commandant of the Guard Jiang Yan fled; Ji took the concurrent post of Commandant of the Guard and assisted Wang Ying in commanding all armies within the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang troops came and Jiang Yan fled, Ji became commandant and aided Wang Ying in city defense.

sentences.zh: 時東昏淫虐，北徐州刺史王珍國就稷謀，乃使直合張齊行弑於含德殿。

translations.literal: At that time Dong Hun was debauched and cruel; Northern Governor of Xu Province Wang Zhenguo consulted Ji, and Ji sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Qi to carry out the assassination in Hede Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hun’s cruelty led Wang Zhenguo and Ji to send Zhang Qi to assassinate him in Hede Hall.

sentences.zh: 稷乃召右僕射王亮等列坐殿前西鍾下，議遣國子博士范雲、中書舍人裴長穆等使石頭城詣武帝，以稷為侍中、左衛將軍，遷大司馬左司馬。

translations.literal: Ji then summoned Right Vice Director Wang Liang and others to sit in a row before the western bell in the hall, deliberating to send National University Doctor Fan Yun and Secretariat Attendant Pei Changmu to Shitou to meet the Emperor, making Ji Attendant and Left Guard General, then transferring him to Senior Aide on the Left of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Ji gathered Wang Liang and others at the western bell and sent Fan Yun and Pei Changmu to Shitou to meet Liang, making Ji attendant and left guard general, then grand marshal senior aide.

sentences.zh: 梁朝建，為散騎常侍，中書令。

translations.literal: When the Liang dynasty was established, he became Regular Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang was founded he became regular attendant and secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 及上即位，封江安縣子，位領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor acceded he enfeoffed Ji as Viscount of Jiang’an and he reached the post of General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: At accession he was enfeoffed viscount of Jiang’an and became general who leads the army.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗于樂壽殿內宴，稷醉後言多怨辭形於色。

translations.literal: The Emperor once feasted in the Hall of Music and Longevity; after Ji was drunk his words were many and resentful and showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Feasting in the Hall of Music and Longevity, drunk Ji spoke resentfully.

sentences.zh: 帝時亦酣，謂曰：「卿兄殺郡守，弟殺其君，袖提帝首，衣染天血，如卿兄弟，有何名稱。

translations.literal: The Emperor was also drunk and said to him, “Your elder brother killed a commandery governor, your younger brother killed his lord; sleeves holding the emperor’s head, clothes stained with heaven’s blood—men like you brothers, what name do you have?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, also drunk, said, “Your brother killed a governor, your brother killed his lord—blood on your sleeves—what name do men like you bear?

sentences.zh: 」稷曰：「臣乃無名稱，至於陛下不得言無勳。

translations.literal: ” Ji said, “I indeed have no name; as for Your Majesty, one cannot say there is no merit.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ji replied, “I have no name; Your Majesty cannot say you lack merit.

sentences.zh: 東昏暴虐，義師亦來伐之，豈在臣而已。

translations.literal: Dong Hun was debauched and cruel; the righteous army also came to attack him—it was not only on my account.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hun was cruel; the righteous army came—not for me alone.

sentences.zh: 」帝埒其須曰：「張公可畏人。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor pinched his beard and said, “Lord Zhang is a man to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor tugged his beard: “Lord Zhang is fearsome.

sentences.zh: 」中丞陸杲彈稷云：「領軍張稷，門無忠貞，官必險達，殺君害主，業以為常。

translations.literal: ” Censor Lu Gao impeached Ji, saying, “General Who Leads the Army Zhang Ji’s house has no loyal constancy; office always reaches through dangerous advancement; killing lords and harming rulers has become his constant trade.
translations.idiomatic: ” Censor Lu Gao impeached Ji for a house without loyalty and a trade in regicide.

sentences.zh: 」武帝留中竟不問。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor kept the memorial within and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor shelved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He rose through the ranks to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 帝將幸稷宅，以盛暑留幸僕射省。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to visit Ji’s residence; because of extreme heat he stayed instead at the Vice Director’s office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to visit Ji’s home but stayed at the vice director’s office in the heat.

sentences.zh: 舊臨幸供具，皆酬太官饌直。

translations.literal: Formerly when the emperor visited, supplies were all paid from the palace kitchen’s food allowance.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial visits were formerly paid from palace kitchen allowances.

sentences.zh: 帝以稷清貧，手詔不受。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Ji was poor and pure, by hand ordered that this not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Calling Ji poor and pure, the emperor refused payment by hand.

sentences.zh: 宋時孝武帝經造張永，至稷三世，並降萬乘，論者榮之。

translations.literal: In Song times Emperor Xiaowu once visited Zhang Yong; down to Ji’s third generation all received the imperial carriage—commentators honored this.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Xiaowu’s visit to Zhang Yong through Ji’s generation, three imperial visits brought commentators’ praise.

sentences.zh: 稷雖居朝右，每慚口實，乃名其子伊字懷尹，霍字希光，畯字農人。

translations.literal: Though Ji held the right of the court, he always felt shame at the talk; he named his sons Yi styled Huaiyin, Huo styled Xiguang, and Jun styled Nongren.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of gossip though high in court, he named sons Yi (Cherish Yin), Huo (Rare Glory), and Jun (Farmer).

sentences.zh: 同字不見，見字不同，以旌其志。

translations.literal: Same character not seen together, seen character not same—thus to display his will.
translations.idiomatic: Characters shared in writing but not in sight displayed his intent.

sentences.zh: 既懼且恨，乃求出，許之。

translations.literal: Both fearful and resentful, he then sought to leave office and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful and resentful, he sought leave and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 出為青冀二州刺史，不得志，常閉合讀佛經。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Qing and Ji Provinces; not achieving his wish, he constantly shut his doors reading Buddhist sutras.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Qing and Ji, frustrated, he shut his doors to read sutras.

sentences.zh: 禁防寬弛，僚吏頗致侵擾。

translations.literal: Defense and prohibitions were lax, and staff officials quite brought about encroachments.
translations.idiomatic: Defenses slackened and staff encroached.

sentences.zh: 州人徐道角等夜襲州城，乃害之。

translations.literal: Men of the province, Xu Daojiao and others, attacked the provincial city by night and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial men led by Xu Daojiao attacked by night and killed him.

sentences.zh: 有司奏削爵土。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized to strip rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: Officials memorialized to strip rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 稷性明烈，善與人交，曆官無畜聚，奉祿皆頒之親故，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Ji by nature was bright and fierce, good at friendship; in successive offices he stored nothing up, and all salary he distributed to kin and friends—his house had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and fierce, he hoarded nothing and gave salary to kin until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 為吳興太守，下車存問遺老，引其子孫置之右職，政稱寬恕。

translations.literal: As Governor of Wuxing, on taking office he inquired after old elders left behind and placed their descendants in honored posts; his governance was called lenient.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuxing he honored old families’ descendants; his rule was called lenient.

sentences.zh: 初去郡就僕射征，道由吳，鄉人候稷者滿水陸。

translations.literal: When he first left the commandery to take up the vice director’s summons, his route passed through Wu; country people waiting for Ji filled land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Wuxing for vice director, Wu countryfolk filled land and water to wait for him.

sentences.zh: 稷單裝徑還都下，人莫之識，其率素如此。

translations.literal: Ji returned alone with simple baggage straight to the capital; no one recognized him—such was his plain simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: He returned alone with simple baggage unrecognized—such was his plainness.

sentences.zh: 稷長女楚媛適會稽孔氏，無子歸宗，至逢稷見害，女以身蔽刃，先父卒。

translations.literal: Ji’s eldest daughter Chuyuan married into the Kong clan of Kuaiji; without a son she returned to her clan; when Ji was killed she shielded the blade with her body and died before her father.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest daughter Chuyuan, childless and returned home, shielded Ji with her body and died first.

sentences.zh: 稷與族兄充、融、卷俱知名，時目云充、融、卷、稷為四張。

translations.literal: Ji and his clan elder cousins Chong, Rong, and Juan were all well known; people of the time regarded Chong, Rong, Juan, and Ji as the Four Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji with cousins Chong, Rong, and Juan were famed as the Four Zhang.

sentences.zh: 卷字令遠，少以和理著稱，能清言，位都官尚書，天監初卒。

translations.literal: Juan, styled Lingyuan, from youth was known for harmony and order, could engage in pure talk, held the post of Director of the Ministry of Justice, and died at the beginning of Tianjian.
translations.idiomatic: Juan, styled Lingyuan, known for harmony and pure talk, headed justice and died early in Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 稷子 嵊

translations.literal: Ji’s son: Sheng
translations.idiomatic: Ji’s son: Sheng

sentences.zh: 嵊字四山。

translations.literal: Sheng, styled Sishan.
translations.idiomatic: His style was Sishan.

sentences.zh: 稷初為剡令，至嵊亭生之，因名嵊，字四山。

translations.literal: When Ji first was Magistrate of Shan, Sheng was born at Sheng Pavilion; therefore he was named Sheng and styled Sishan.
translations.idiomatic: Born at Sheng Pavilion when Ji was magistrate of Shan, he was named Sheng, styled Sishan.

sentences.zh: 少敦孝行，年三十餘，猶斑衣受稷杖，動至數百，收淚歡然。

translations.literal: From youth he cultivated filial conduct; though over thirty he still wore variegated clothes receiving Ji’s beating, up to several hundred strokes, then wiping tears he was joyful.
translations.idiomatic: Past thirty he still wore child’s dress for Ji’s beatings—hundreds of strokes—then wept and smiled.

sentences.zh: 方雅有志操，能清言，感家禍，終身蔬食布衣，手不執刀刃，不聽音樂。

translations.literal: Upright and refined with purpose, he could engage in pure talk; moved by family calamity, all his life he ate vegetables and wore cloth, never held a blade, and never listened to music.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and pure-talking, family tragedy made him vegetarian, cloth-clad, bladeless, and musicless for life.

sentences.zh: 弟淮言氣不倫，嵊垂泣訓誘。

translations.literal: Younger brother Huai’s speech and spirit were unbalanced; Sheng wept and admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: When brother Huai’s conduct faltered, Sheng wept and admonished him.

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，累遷鎮南湘東王長史、尋陽太守。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretary Lang and rose through the ranks to Senior Aide to Prince of Xiangdong of the South and Governor of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from secretary lang to senior aide to Prince of Xiangdong and governor of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 王暇日玄言，因為之筮，得節卦，謂嵊曰：「卿後當東入為郡，恐不得終其天年。

translations.literal: On the prince’s leisure days in abstruse talk he cast the hexagrams for Sheng and obtained Jie; he told Sheng, “Later you will go east to govern a commandery and I fear you will not complete your natural years.
translations.idiomatic: The prince divined Jie for Sheng and said, “You will govern eastward but may not live out your years.

sentences.zh: 」嵊曰：「貴得其所耳。

translations.literal: ” Sheng said, “Noble attainment of one’s place is enough.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sheng said, “Dying in the right place is enough.

sentences.zh: 」時伏挺在坐，曰：「君王可畏人也。」

translations.literal: ” Fu Ting was present and said, “My lord is a man to be feared.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu Ting said, “My lord is fearsome.”

sentences.zh: 還為太府卿，吳興太守。

translations.literal: He returned to be Director of the Grand Storehouse and Governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as grand storehouse director and Wuxing governor.

sentences.zh: 侯景圍建鄴，遣弟伊率郡兵赴援。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing besieged Jiankang, he sent younger brother Yi to lead commandery troops to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing besieged Jiankang he sent brother Yi with commandery troops.

sentences.zh: 城陷，御史中丞沈浚違難東歸，嵊往見之，謂曰：「賊臣憑陵，人臣效命之日，今欲收集兵刃，保據貴鄉，雖復萬死，誠亦無恨。

translations.literal: After the city fell, Censor-in-Chief Shen Jun fled east; Sheng went to see him and said, “The rebel minister towers over us; the day a minister gives his life is today—now I wish to gather weapons and hold your noble district; though death ten thousand times over, truly I have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall Sheng told fleeing Shen Jun, “Today ministers die—I will gather arms and hold your district without regret.

sentences.zh: 」浚固勸嵊舉義。

translations.literal: ” Jun firmly urged Sheng to raise the righteous banner.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jun urged him to raise the righteous banner.

sentences.zh: 時邵陵王綸東奔至錢唐，聞之，遣前舍人陸丘公板授嵊征東將軍。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Shaoling Lun fled east to Qiantang; hearing this, he sent former Attendant Lu Qiugong to appoint Sheng General Who Conquers the East by written tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shaoling Lun, fleeing to Qiantang, sent Lu Qiugong to appoint Sheng general who conquers the east by tablet.

sentences.zh: 嵊曰：「天子蒙塵，今日何情復受榮號。

translations.literal: Sheng said, “The Son of Heaven is in dust and exile—what mood is there now to receive honored titles?
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, “The emperor is in exile—what honor is there in titles now?

sentences.zh: 」留板而已。

translations.literal: ” He kept only the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: ” He kept the tablet only.

sentences.zh: 賊行台劉神茂攻破義興，遣使說嵊，嵊斬其使，仍遣軍破神茂。

translations.literal: The rebel field headquarters Liu Shenmao broke Yixing; he sent an envoy to persuade Sheng, and Sheng beheaded the envoy and still sent troops to defeat Shenmao.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Liu Shenmao took Yixing; Sheng beheaded his envoy and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 侯景乃遣其中軍侯子鑒助神茂擊嵊。

translations.literal: Hou Jing then sent his Central Army Hou Zijian to assist Shenmao in attacking Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sent Hou Zijian to aid Shenmao against Sheng.

sentences.zh: 嵊軍敗，乃釋戎服坐於聽事。

translations.literal: Sheng’s army was defeated; he then doffed armor and sat in the reception hall.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, Sheng doffed armor and sat in the hall.

sentences.zh: 賊臨以刃終不屈，執以送景。

translations.literal: The rebels pressed him with blades yet he would not yield; they seized him and sent him to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Blades at his throat could not bend him; they sent him to Jing.

sentences.zh: 景將舍之，嵊曰：「速死為幸。

translations.literal: Jing was about to spare him; Sheng said, “Swift death is fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Jing meant to spare him; Sheng said, “Quick death is mercy.

sentences.zh: 」乃殺之。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was killed.

sentences.zh: 子弟遇害者十餘人。

translations.literal: More than ten sons and younger brothers met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten sons and brothers died with him.

sentences.zh: 景欲存其一子嵊曰：「吾一門已在鬼錄，不就爾處求恩。

translations.literal: Jing wished to spare one son; Sheng said, “My whole house is already on the ghost register—I will not seek favor from you.
translations.idiomatic: Jing offered to spare a son; Sheng said, “My house is already dead—I want no favor from you.

sentences.zh: 」於是皆死。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon all died.
translations.idiomatic: ” All died.

sentences.zh: 賊平，元帝追贈侍中、中衛將軍、開府儀同三司，諡忠貞子。

translations.literal: After the rebels were pacified, Emperor Yuan posthumously gave him Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Central Guard, Grand Marshal with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies, and posthumous title Zhongzhenzi.
translations.idiomatic: After rebels fell, Emperor Yuan posthumously made him attendant, central guard general, and grand marshal titled Zhongzhenzi.

sentences.zh: 嵊弟睾知名。

translations.literal: Sheng’s younger brother Gao was well known.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng’s younger brother Gao was celebrated.

sentences.zh: 永從孫 種

translations.literal: Yong’s grandnephew: Zhong
translations.idiomatic: Grandnephew of Yong: Zhong

sentences.zh: 種字士苗，永從孫也。

translations.literal: Zhong, styled Shimiao, was Yong’s grandnephew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shimiao descended from Yong’s line.

sentences.zh: 祖辯，宋大司農，廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bian was Grand Minister of Agriculture and Governor of Guang Province in Song.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Bian was Song’s grand minister of agriculture and governor of Guang.

sentences.zh: 父略，太子中庶子，臨海太守。

translations.literal: His father Lue was Senior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Governor of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Father Lue was senior mentor of the heir apparent and governor of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 種少恬靜，居處雅正，傍無造請。

translations.literal: Zhong from youth was tranquil; his dwelling and conduct were refined and upright, and none came to visit on private business.
translations.idiomatic: Tranquil from youth, he lived uprightly and received no private callers.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「宋稱敷、演，梁則卷、充，清虛學尚，種有其風。

translations.literal: People of the time said, “Under Song, Fu and Yan were praised; under Liang, Juan and Chong—pure learning and lofty conduct, Zhong has that wind.
translations.idiomatic: People said, “Song praised Fu and Yan; Liang praises Juan and Chong—pure learning lives in Zhong.

sentences.zh: 」仕梁為中軍宣城王府主簿，時已四十餘。

translations.literal: ” He served Liang as Chief Clerk on Prince of Xuancheng’s staff when he was already over forty.
translations.idiomatic: ” He served Liang as Prince of Xuancheng’s chief clerk after forty.

sentences.zh: 家貧，求為始豐令。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he sought to be Magistrate of Shifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he sought magistracy of Shifeng.

sentences.zh: 及武陵王紀為益州刺史，重選府僚，以種為左西曹掾。

translations.literal: When Prince of Wuling Ji was Governor of Yi Province and carefully chose staff, Zhong was made Senior Aide of the Left in the Western Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wuling Ji, governing Yi, chose Zhong as left senior aide.

sentences.zh: 種辭以母老，為有司奏，坐黜免。

translations.literal: Zhong declined because his mother was old; the relevant office memorialized and he was dismissed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: He declined for his aged mother and was dismissed by memorial.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，奉母東奔鄉里。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing’s rebellion he led his mother east to their home district.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing’s rebellion he fled east with his mother.

sentences.zh: 母卒，種時年五十，而毀瘠過甚。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Zhong was then fifty, yet his emaciation was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: At fifty when his mother died his grief-wasting was extreme.

sentences.zh: 又迫以凶荒未葬，服雖畢，居家飲食，恒若在喪。

translations.literal: He was also pressed because famine prevented burial; though mourning ended, at home in eating and drinking he was always as if in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Famine delayed burial; after mourning ended he still ate and lived as mourner.

sentences.zh: 景平，初司徒王僧辯以狀奏，起為中從事，並為具葬禮，葬訖，種方即吉。

translations.literal: After Jing was pacified, Minister of Ceremonies Wang Sengbian first memorialized on his condition and appointed him Middle Attendant, also providing full burial rites; only after burial did Zhong put off mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing’s fall Wang Sengbian restored him as middle attendant, provided burial, and only then did Zhong end mourning.

sentences.zh: 僧辯又以種年老無子，賜以妾及居處之具。

translations.literal: Sengbian also, because Zhong was old and without a son, bestowed a concubine and furnishings for dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian also gave him a concubine and a dwelling since he was old and childless.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受禪，為太常卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen received the abdication, Zhong became Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen accepted the throne, Zhong became minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 歷位左戶尚書，侍中，中書令，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Director of the Left Household Ministry, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: He successively headed left household, attended, directed the secretariat, and became golden-seal grand master.

sentences.zh: 種沈深虛靜，識量宏博，時以為宰相之器。

translations.literal: Zhong was deep, empty, and still, with broad judgment; people of the time considered him material for chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Deep, still, and broad-minded, he was seen as chief-minister material.

sentences.zh: 僕射徐陵嘗抗表讓位於種，以為宜居左執，其為所推如此。

translations.literal: Vice Director Xu Ling once submitted a memorial yielding place to Zhong, holding that he should occupy the left seat; such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Ling once yielded the left seat to him—such was his esteem.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈特進，諡元子。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given Special Advance and posthumous title Yuanzi.
translations.idiomatic: He died posthumously titled Yuanzi with special advance.

sentences.zh: 種仁恕寡欲，雖曆顯位，家產屢空，終日晏然，不以為病。

translations.literal: Zhong was humane, forgiving, and with few desires; though he held prominent posts repeatedly, his household property was often empty, yet all day he was at ease and did not take it as affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Humane and wanting little, he held high office yet stayed empty and untroubled.

sentences.zh: 太建初，女為始興王妃，以居處僻陋，特賜宅一區。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taijian his daughter became princess of Shixing; because her dwelling was cramped, she was specially granted one residence.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian 1 his daughter became princess of Shixing and received a house for cramped quarters.

sentences.zh: 又累賜無錫、嘉興縣秩。

translations.literal: He was also repeatedly granted the salary of Wuxi and Jiaxing counties.
translations.idiomatic: He also received repeated grants of Wuxi and Jiaxing salaries.

sentences.zh: 嘗於無錫見重囚在獄，天寒，呼囚暴日，遂失之，帝大笑而不深責。

translations.literal: Once at Wuxi he saw heavy prisoners in jail; the day was cold and he called prisoners out to sun themselves, and they escaped—the Emperor laughed greatly and did not punish deeply.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuxi he sunned prisoners who then escaped; the emperor laughed and did not punish harshly.

sentences.zh: 有集十四卷。

translations.literal: He had collected works in fourteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran fourteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 種弟棱亦清靜有識度，位司徒左長史，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Zhong’s younger brother Leng was also pure and still with judgment, holding the post of Senior Aide of the Left in the Secretariat and posthumously given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Leng was also pure and judged well, ending as left senior aide and posthumous grand master.

sentences.zh: 論曰：張裕有宋之初，早參霸政，出內所曆，莫非清顯，諸子並荷崇構，克舉家聲，其美譽所歸，豈徒然也。

translations.literal: Commentary says: At the beginning of Song, Zhang Yu early joined the hegemonic government; in every post within and without the court none was not pure and prominent, and the sons all received lofty structure and upheld the family’s reputation—the renown to which their beauty returned—was it merely for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: At Song’s founding Zhang Yu joined the hegemonic regime; every post was honorable, sons upheld the house—such renown was earned.

sentences.zh: 思曼立身簡素，殆人望乎。

translations.literal: Siman established himself in plain simplicity—was it not the people’s expectation?
translations.idiomatic: Siman lived in plain simplicity—the people’s hope indeed.

sentences.zh: 夫濯纓從事，理存無二，取信一主，義絕百心。

translations.literal: To wash the tassel and serve in office— principle admits no duality; to give faith to one lord is to sever the heart from a hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: Washing the tassel to serve one lord ends divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 以永元之末，人憂塗炭，公喬重圍之內，首創大謀，而旋見猜嫌，又況異於斯也。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan, when men feared charcoal on the road, Gongqiao within heavy siege first launched the great plan, yet soon met suspicion—how much more when different from this!
translations.idiomatic: At Yongyuan’s end, amid universal fear, Gongqiao launched the great plot under siege yet met suspicion—how much worse when loyalties differ!

sentences.zh: 然則士之行己，可無深議。

translations.literal: Yet then a gentleman’s conduct in preserving himself—one need not judge deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a gentleman’s self-preservation need not be judged harshly.

sentences.zh: 四山赴蹈之方，可謂矯其違矣。

translations.literal: Sishan’s way of going forward and treading down—one may say he corrected their deviation.
translations.idiomatic: Sishan’s path of courageous death corrected their deviation.
